bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十一】起重光大淵獻，盡閼逢攝提格，凡四年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 21] Beginning with Chongguang Dayuanxian and ending with Yanfeng Shetige, altogether four years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 21] This section covers four years, from the cyclical year Chongguang Dayuanxian through Yanfeng Shetige.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁酉，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day dingyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, in the first month on the day dingyou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 苻健左長史賈玄碩等請依劉備稱漢中王故事，表健為都督關中諸軍事、大將軍、大單于、秦王。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's Left Chief Clerk Jia Xuanshuo and others asked to follow the precedent of Liu Bei proclaiming himself King of Hanzhong, and memorialized that Jian be made Grand Commander of All Military Affairs in Guanzhong, Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuanshuo, Fu Jian's chief clerk on the left, and others urged him to follow Liu Bei's precedent in taking the title King of Hanzhong, and submitted a memorial appointing Jian Grand Commander of Guanzhong forces, Grand General, Great Chanyu, and King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 健怒曰：「吾豈堪為秦王邪！

translations.literal: Jian said angrily, "How could I be fit to be King of Qin!
translations.idiomatic: Jian flew into a rage. "How dare you think me worthy of being King of Qin!

sentences.zh: 且晉使未返，我之官爵，非汝曹所知也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Jin envoy has not yet returned; my titles and ranks are not for you lot to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Jin envoy has not even returned yet—my rank and titles are none of your business."

sentences.zh: 」既而密使梁安諷玄碩等上尊號，健辭讓再三，然後許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he secretly sent Liang An to prompt Xuanshuo and the others to submit an exalted title; Jian declined repeatedly, and only then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly, however, he sent Liang An to coax Xuanshuo and the rest into pressing a higher title upon him. Jian refused three times before at last accepting.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，健即天王、大單于位，國號大秦，大赦，改元皇始。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Jian assumed the positions of Heavenly King and Great Chanyu; the state was named Great Qin; a general amnesty was declared; the era name was changed to Huangshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Jian took the throne as Heavenly King and Great Chanyu, named his realm Great Qin, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Huangshi.

sentences.zh: 追尊父洪為武惠皇帝，廟號太祖；

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Hong as Emperor Wuhui, with the temple name Taizu;
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously ennobled his father Hong as Emperor Wuhui, with the temple name Taizu;

sentences.zh: 立妻強氏為天王后，子萇為太子，靚為平原公，生為淮南公，覿為長樂公，方為高陽公，碩為北平公，騰為淮陽公，柳為晉公，桐為汝南公，廋為魏公，武為燕公，幼為趙公。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Qiang as Heavenly Queen; his son Chang as Crown Prince; Jing as Duke of Pingyuan; Sheng as Duke of Huainan; Di as Duke of Changle; Fang as Duke of Gaoyang; Shuo as Duke of Beiping; Teng as Duke of Huaiyang; Liu as Duke of Jin; Tong as Duke of Runan; Sou as Duke of Wei; Wu as Duke of Yan; and You as Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Qiang became Heavenly Queen; Chang was named crown prince; and his sons received ducal titles—Jing as Duke of Pingyuan, Sheng of Huainan, Di of Changle, Fang of Gaoyang, Shuo of Beiping, Teng of Huaiyang, Liu of Jin, Tong of Runan, Sou of Wei, Wu of Yan, and You of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以苻雄為都督中外諸軍事、丞相、領車騎大將軍、雍州牧、東海公；

translations.literal: He appointed Fu Xiong Grand Commander of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Chancellor, concurrently General of Chariots and Cavalry, Governor of Yong Province, and Duke of Donghai;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong was made supreme commander of all armies at home and abroad, chancellor, general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Yong Province, and Duke of Donghai;

sentences.zh: 苻菁為衛大將軍、平昌公，宿衛二宮；

translations.literal: Fu Jing was made Defender Grand General and Duke of Pingchang, guarding both palaces;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jing became defender-in-chief and Duke of Pingchang, charged with guarding both palaces;

sentences.zh: 雷弱兒為太尉，毛貴為司空，略陽姜伯周為尚書令，梁楞為左僕射，王墮為右僕射，魚遵為太子太師，強平為太傅，段純為太保，呂婆樓為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Lei Ruo'er was made Grand Commandant; Mao Gui Minister of Works; Jiang Bozhou of Lueyang Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Liang Leng Left Vice Director; Wang Duo Right Vice Director; Yu Zun Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; Qiang Ping Grand Mentor; Duan Chun Grand Guardian; and Lü Polou Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ruo'er became grand commandant; Mao Gui minister of works; Jiang Bozhou of Lueyang director of the secretariat; Liang Leng and Wang Duo left and right vice directors; Yu Zun grand tutor to the heir; Qiang Ping grand mentor; Duan Chun grand guardian; and Lü Polou attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 伯周，健之舅；

translations.literal: Bozhou was Jian's maternal uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou was Jian's uncle on his mother's side;

sentences.zh: 平，王后之弟；

translations.literal: Ping was the queen's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Ping was the queen's brother;

sentences.zh: 婆樓，本略陽氐酋也。

translations.literal: Polou had originally been a Di chieftain of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Polou had once been a Di tribal chief in Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 段龕請以青州內附；

translations.literal: Duan Kan asked to submit Qing Province and come under Qin rule;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Kan offered to bring Qing Province over to Qin allegiance;

sentences.zh: 二月，戊寅，以龕為鎮北將軍，封齊公。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day wuyin, Kan was made General Who Pacifies the North and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day wuyin, Kan was appointed general who pacifies the north and created Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔攻圍襄國百餘日，趙主祗危急，乃去皇帝之號，稱趙王；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Min had besieged Xiangguo for more than a hundred days; the Zhao ruler Zhi was in dire straits, and therefore relinquished the title of emperor and styled himself King of Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Min had kept Xiangguo under siege for over a hundred days. Zhao ruler Zhi, hard pressed, dropped the imperial title and called himself merely King of Zhao;

sentences.zh: 遣太尉張舉乞師於燕，許送傳國璽，中軍將軍張春乞師於姚弋仲。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Commandant Zhang Ju to beg troops from Yan, promising to deliver the imperial seal; Central Army General Zhang Chun begged troops from Yao Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Commandant Zhang Ju to Yan to plead for aid, promising the imperial seal in return, while Central Army General Zhang Chun sought help from Yao Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 弋仲遣其子襄帥騎二萬八千救趙，誡之曰：「冉閔棄仁背義，屠滅石氏。

translations.literal: Yizhong sent his son Xiang leading twenty-eight thousand horsemen to rescue Zhao, admonishing him, "Ran Min abandoned benevolence and betrayed righteousness, slaughtering and wiping out the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong dispatched his son Xiang at the head of twenty-eight thousand cavalry to save Zhao, with this charge: "Ran Min has cast aside duty and betrayed his patrons, exterminating the house of Shi.

sentences.zh: 我受人厚遇，當為復仇，老病不能自行；

translations.literal: I received great kindness from them and ought to take revenge; I am old and ill and cannot go in person;
translations.idiomatic: They showed me great favor, and revenge is owed—but I am old and sick and cannot ride out myself;

sentences.zh: 汝才十倍於閔，若不梟擒以來，不必復見我也！

translations.literal: your talent is ten times Min's—if you do not bring him back as a captive with his head displayed, you need not see me again!"
translations.idiomatic: you are ten times the man Min is. Unless you bring him back in chains with his head on a pole, do not come back to me!"

sentences.zh: 」弋仲亦遣使告於燕，燕主俊遣御難將軍悅綰將兵三萬往會之。

translations.literal: Yizhong also sent envoys to inform Yan; the Yan ruler Jun sent the general who withstands difficulty, Yue Chuo, with thirty thousand troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong also notified Yan. Yan ruler Jun sent General Yue Chuo with thirty thousand men to link up with the relief force.

sentences.zh: 冉閔聞俊欲救趙，遣大司馬從事中郎廣寧常煒使於燕。

translations.literal: When Ran Min heard that Jun intended to rescue Zhao, he sent Attendant Gentleman of the Grand Marshal's Staff, Chang Wei of Guangning, as envoy to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jun meant to rescue Zhao, Ran Min dispatched Chang Wei of Guangning, an attendant in the grand marshal's office, to Yan as his envoy.

sentences.zh: 俊使封裕詰之曰：「冉閔，石氏養息，負恩作逆，何敢輒稱大號？

translations.literal: Jun had Feng Yu interrogate him, saying, "Ran Min was a foster son raised by the Shi clan; he repaid kindness with rebellion—how dare he presumptuously assume a grand title?
translations.idiomatic: Jun had Feng Yu challenge him: "Ran Min was a ward of the Shi family who repaid their kindness with treason—how dare he take a sovereign title for himself?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「湯放桀，武王伐紂，以興商、周之業；

translations.literal: Wei replied, "Tang banished Jie; King Wu attacked Zhou—thereby they raised up the enterprises of Shang and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wei answered, "Tang drove out Jie; King Wu overthrew Zhou—by such acts the houses of Shang and Zhou rose to power;

sentences.zh: 曹孟德養於宦官，莫知所出，卒立魏氏之基。

translations.literal: Cao Mengde was raised among eunuchs; no one knew his origin, yet in the end he laid the foundation of the Wei house.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was brought up in a eunuch's household; no one knew his birth, yet he founded the Wei dynasty in the end.

sentences.zh: 苟非天命，安能成功！

translations.literal: If it were not the Mandate of Heaven, how could they have succeeded!
translations.idiomatic: Without Heaven's mandate, how could any of them have triumphed?

sentences.zh: 推此而言，何必致問！

translations.literal: Extending this reasoning, why must you press the question!
translations.idiomatic: By that logic, why press the point at all?

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「人言冉閔初立，鑄金為己像，以卜成敗，而像不成，信乎？

translations.literal: Yu said, "People say that when Ran Min first took the throne he cast a gold image of himself to divine success or failure, and the image would not form—is that true?
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "People say that when Ran Min first seized power he cast a golden statue of himself to test his fortune, and the statue would not take shape—is that so?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「不聞。

translations.literal: Wei said, "I have not heard of it."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "I have heard nothing of the sort."

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「南來者皆云如是，何故隱之？

translations.literal: Yu said, "Everyone coming from the south says it is so—why conceal it?
translations.idiomatic: Yu pressed him: "Every traveler from the south says the same—why hide it?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「奸偽之人欲矯天命以惑人者，乃假符瑞、托蓍龜以自重，魏主握符璽，據中州，受命何疑；

translations.literal: Wei said, "Treacherous and false men who wish to twist the Mandate of Heaven to mislead others borrow omens and rely on milfoil and tortoise to aggrandize themselves. The Wei ruler holds the tally and seal and occupies the Central Plains—how can there be doubt that he has received the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied, "Fraudsters who twist Heaven's will to deceive the people invent portents and lean on divination to puff themselves up. Our lord holds the imperial regalia and rules the heartland—his mandate is beyond question;

sentences.zh: 而更反真為偽，取決於金像乎！

translations.literal: yet you would turn truth into falsehood and decide the matter by a golden statue!
translations.idiomatic: yet you would call truth falsehood and judge him by a golden idol!

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「傳國璽果安在？

translations.literal: Yu said, "Where in truth is the imperial transmission seal?
translations.idiomatic: Yu asked, "Where is the imperial seal, really?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「在鄴」。

translations.literal: Wei said, "It is at Ye."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "At Ye."

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「張舉言在襄國。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Zhang Ju says it is at Xiangguo."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Zhang Ju claims it is at Xiangguo."

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「殺胡之日，在鄴者殆無孑遺；

translations.literal: Wei said, "On the day the Hu were slaughtered, scarcely a single survivor remained in Ye;
translations.idiomatic: Wei answered, "On the day of the Hu massacre, almost no one was left alive in Ye;

sentences.zh: 時有迸漏者，皆潛伏溝瀆中耳，彼安知璽之所在乎！

translations.literal: those who escaped by chance all hid in ditches and drains—how would they know where the seal was!
translations.idiomatic: any who slipped through the net cowered in ditches and drains—what would they know of where the seal lay!

sentences.zh: 彼求救者，為妄誕之辭，無所不可，況一璽乎！

translations.literal: Those begging for rescue will utter any wild fabrication—nothing is too much, let alone a single seal!
translations.idiomatic: Men begging for rescue will say anything—no lie is too bold, and a seal is the least of it!

sentences.zh: 俊猶以張舉之言為信，乃積柴其旁，使裕以其私誘之，曰：「君更熟思，無為徒取灰滅！

translations.literal: Jun still believed Zhang Ju's words, and piled firewood beside Wei; he had Yu tempt him privately, saying, "Consider again carefully—do not bring ruin upon yourself for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: Jun still trusted Zhang Ju, so he heaped firewood beside the envoy and had Yu speak to him privately: "Think again—do not throw your life away for nothing!

sentences.zh: 」煒正色曰：「石氏貪暴，親帥大兵攻燕國都。

translations.literal: Wei said sternly, "The Shi clan was greedy and violent; they personally led a great army to attack the Yan capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei answered with a grave face, "The Shi were rapacious and cruel—they led a great host in person against your capital.

sentences.zh: 雖不克而返，然志在必取。

translations.literal: Though they did not take it and withdrew, their intent was fixed on seizing it.
translations.idiomatic: They failed and withdrew, but their aim was still to conquer you.

sentences.zh: 故運資糧、聚器械於東北者，非以相資，乃欲相滅也。

translations.literal: Therefore the transport of provisions and gathering of weapons in the northeast was not to aid you but to destroy you.
translations.idiomatic: The grain and arms they moved into the northeast were not to help Yan but to destroy it.

sentences.zh: 魏主誅剪石氏，雖不為燕，臣子之心，聞仇讎之滅，義當如何？

translations.literal: The Wei ruler executed and uprooted the Shi clan—not for Yan's sake, yet in the heart of a subject, hearing that a foe is destroyed, what is proper conduct?
translations.idiomatic: Our lord destroyed the house of Shi—not for Yan's benefit, yet what loyal subject would not rejoice when an enemy falls?

sentences.zh: 而更為彼責我，不亦異乎！

translations.literal: Yet you blame me on their account—is that not strange!
translations.idiomatic: And now you reproach me in their name—is that not perverse!

sentences.zh: 吾聞死者骨肉下於土，精魂升於天。

translations.literal: I have heard that when a man dies his flesh and bones go down into the earth and his vital spirit rises to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when a man dies his body returns to earth and his spirit ascends to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 蒙君之惠，速益薪縱火，使僕得上訴於帝足矣！

translations.literal: Thanks to your kindness, if you quickly add fuel and set the fire, so that I may lodge my appeal with the Emperor above, that is enough!
translations.idiomatic: Do me the kindness to pile on the wood and light the flame at once—that I may plead my case before Heaven is all I ask!

sentences.zh: 」左右請殺之，俊曰：「彼不憚殺身而徇其主，忠臣也！

translations.literal: Those beside him asked to kill him; Jun said, "He does not fear death in serving his lord—a loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged execution. Jun said, "He does not shrink from death in serving his master—a true loyalist!

sentences.zh: 且冉閔有罪，使臣何預焉！

translations.literal: Moreover Ran Min is guilty—what has the envoy to do with it!
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min may be guilty, but what has his envoy done!

sentences.zh: 」使出就館。

translations.literal: He had Wei sent out to the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wei back to the guest quarters.

sentences.zh: 夜，使其鄉人趙瞻往勞之，且曰：「君何不以實言？

translations.literal: At night he sent his fellow townsman Zhao Zhan to comfort Wei, saying, "Why do you not speak the truth?
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent a fellow townsman, Zhao Zhan, to visit Wei and said, "Why not tell the plain truth?

sentences.zh: 王怒，欲處君於遼、碣之表，奈何？

translations.literal: The king is angry and wishes to banish you beyond Liao and Jie—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: The king is furious and means to send you beyond the Liao and Jie ranges—what then?

sentences.zh: 」煒曰：「吾結髮以來，尚不欺布衣，況人主乎！

translations.literal: Wei said, "Since I bound up my hair I have not deceived even a commoner—how much less a sovereign!
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Since I came of age I have not lied even to a commoner—still less to a king!

sentences.zh: 曲意苟合，性所不能。

translations.literal: To bend my meaning and seek accommodation is something my nature cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Bending the truth to please others is not in my nature.

sentences.zh: 直情盡言，雖沉東海，不敢避也！

translations.literal: To speak my mind fully—even if drowned in the eastern sea, I would not shrink from it!
translations.idiomatic: I will speak plainly, even if I must sink to the bottom of the eastern sea—I will not flinch!

sentences.zh: 」遂臥向壁，不復與瞻言。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lay down facing the wall and would speak with Zhan no more.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the wall and would not speak to Zhan again.

sentences.zh: 瞻具以白俊，俊乃囚煒於龍城。

translations.literal: Zhan reported everything to Jun, and Jun then imprisoned Wei in Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan reported all this to Jun, who had Wei imprisoned in Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 趙并州刺史張平遣使降秦，秦王以平為大將軍、冀州牧。

translations.literal: Zhang Ping, Inspector of Bing Province in Zhao, sent envoys to submit to Qin; the King of Qin appointed Ping Grand General and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ping, Zhao's inspector of Bing Province, sent envoys to surrender to Qin; the Qin king made him grand general and governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 燕王逡還薊。

translations.literal: The King of Yan hesitantly withdrew to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king lingered, then withdrew to Ji.

sentences.zh: 三月，姚襄及趙汝陰王琨各引兵救襄國。

translations.literal: In the third month, Yao Xiang and the Zhao Prince of Ruyin, Kun, each led troops to relieve Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Yao Xiang and Zhao's Prince of Ruyin, Kun, each marched to relieve Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 冉閔遣車騎將軍胡睦拒襄於長蘆，將軍孫威拒琨於黃丘，皆敗還，士卒略盡。

translations.literal: Ran Min sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Hu Mu to block Xiang at Changlu and General Sun Wei to block Kun at Huangqiu; both were defeated and withdrew, their soldiers nearly all lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min sent Hu Mu to hold Xiang at Changlu and Sun Wei to hold Kun at Huangqiu; both were beaten back with their forces all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 閔欲自出擊之，衛將軍王泰諫曰：「今襄國未下，外救雲集，若我出戰，必覆背受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Min wished to go out and attack them in person; Defender General Wang Tai remonstrated, "Xiangguo is not yet taken and outside relief is gathering like clouds; if we go out to battle we shall surely be caught front and rear—this is a perilous course.
translations.idiomatic: Min meant to lead the counterattack himself. Defender-in-chief Wang Tai urged caution: "Xiangguo still stands, and relief armies are massing. If we march out we risk attack from front and rear—that is a deadly gamble.

sentences.zh: 不若固壘以挫其銳，徐觀其釁而擊之。

translations.literal: Better to hold the walls and blunt their edge, then watch for an opening and strike.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the fortifications, wear down their momentum, and strike when they show a weakness.

sentences.zh: 且陛下親臨行陳，如失萬全，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Moreover if Your Majesty personally goes to the battle line and the least mishap occurs, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: And if Your Majesty takes the field in person, one slip could cost you the realm.

sentences.zh: 」閔將止，道士法饒進曰：「陛下圍襄國經年，無尺寸之功，今賊至，又避不擊，將何以使將士乎！

translations.literal: Min was about to stop when the Daoist Fa Rao advanced and said, "Your Majesty has besieged Xiangguo for a year without the slightest gain; now the enemy has come and again you avoid battle—how will you command the officers and soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: Min was about to relent when the Daoist Fa Rao spoke up: "You have besieged Xiangguo for a year without gain. The enemy is here and you shrink from fighting—how will you lead your men?

sentences.zh: 且太白入昴，當殺胡王，百戰百克，不可失也！

translations.literal: Moreover Taibai has entered the Mao constellation—this means the Hu king must be killed; in a hundred battles a hundred victories—this chance must not be lost!
translations.idiomatic: Taibai has entered the Mao lodge—the Hu king is marked for death. Victory is certain; do not miss this moment!

sentences.zh: 」閔攘袂大言曰：「吾戰決矣，敢沮眾者斬！

translations.literal: Min rolled up his sleeves and declared loudly, "My mind is set on battle—whoever dares discourage the host shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Min threw back his sleeves and thundered, "I have decided to fight! Anyone who discourages the army dies!

sentences.zh: 」乃悉眾出，與襄、琨戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led out his entire force and fought Xiang and Kun.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out with his whole army to meet Xiang and Kun in battle.

sentences.zh: 悅綰適以燕兵至，去魏兵數里，疏布騎卒，曳柴揚塵，魏人望之恟懼，襄、琨、綰三面擊之，趙王祗自後沖之，魏兵大敗，閔與十餘騎走還鄴。

translations.literal: Yue Chuo happened to arrive with Yan troops a few li from the Wei army; he spread out his horsemen loosely, dragged brush to raise dust, and the Wei men seeing this were panic-stricken; Xiang, Kun, and Chuo attacked on three sides, and Zhao King Zhi charged from the rear; the Wei army was utterly defeated, and Min fled back to Ye with a dozen or so horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Chuo arrived just then with Yan cavalry a few li away. He spread his riders thin, dragged brush to raise dust, and the Wei troops panicked at the sight. Xiang, Kun, and Chuo struck from three sides while Zhao king Zhi charged from behind. The Wei army collapsed; Min escaped to Ye with barely a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 降胡栗特康等執大單于胤及左僕射劉琦以降趙，趙王祗殺之。

translations.literal: The surrendered Hu Li Tekang and others seized the Great Chanyu Yin and Left Vice Director Liu Qi and surrendered them to Zhao; Zhao King Zhi killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Hu soldiers led by Li Tekang seized Great Chanyu Yin and Vice Director Liu Qi and handed them to Zhao; Zhi had them executed.

sentences.zh: 胡睦及司空石璞、尚書令徐機、中書監盧諶等並將士死者凡十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Hu Mu and Minister of Works Shi Pu, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Ji, Palace Secretary Lu Chen, and officers and soldiers who died numbered more than a hundred thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mu, Shi Pu, Xu Ji, Lu Chen, and the rest fell with more than a hundred thousand soldiers dead.

sentences.zh: 閔潛還，人無知者。

translations.literal: Min returned secretly and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Min slipped back into the city without anyone knowing.

sentences.zh: 鄴另震恐，訛言閔已沒。

translations.literal: Ye was thrown into terror; rumor spread that Min had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Panic gripped Ye; rumors spread that Min was dead.

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉張艾請閔親郊以安眾心。

translations.literal: Commandant of Archers Zhang Ai asked Min to perform the suburban sacrifice in person to steady the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Archers Zhang Ai urged Min to perform the suburban sacrifice in person to calm the people.

sentences.zh: 閔從之，訛言乃息。

translations.literal: Min complied, and the rumors then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Min agreed, and the rumors subsided.

sentences.zh: 閔支解法饒父子，贈韋謏大司徒。

translations.literal: Min dismembered Fa Rao and his son by execution; he posthumously honored Wei Xu as Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Min had Fa Rao and his son torn apart by horses and posthumously honored Wei Xu as grand steward.

sentences.zh: 姚襄還還灄頭，姚弋仲怒其不擒閔，杖之一百。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang returned to Santou; Yao Yizhong was angry that he had not captured Min and had him beaten a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang withdrew to Santou. Yizhong, furious that he had failed to capture Min, had him flogged a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 初，閔之為趙相也，悉散倉庫以樹私恩，與羌、胡相攻，無月不戰。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Min was chancellor of Zhao, he emptied the storehouses entirely to cultivate private favor; he fought with the Qiang and Hu month after month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Zhao's chancellor, Min had emptied the treasuries to buy loyalty and fought the Qiang and Hu almost every month.

sentences.zh: 趙所徙青、雍、幽、荊四州人民及氐、羌、胡蠻數百萬口，以趙法禁不行，各還本土；

translations.literal: The millions of people of Qing, Yong, You, and Jing provinces whom Zhao had relocated, and the Di, Qiang, Hu, and other tribes—because Zhao's laws and prohibitions no longer held—each returned to their homelands;
translations.idiomatic: Millions relocated from Qing, Yong, You, and Jing, along with Di, Qiang, Hu, and other peoples, turned homeward once Zhao's authority collapsed;

sentences.zh: 道路交錯，互相殺掠，其能達者什有二、三。

translations.literal: the roads crisscrossed with flight and mutual slaughter; of those who could reach their destinations only two or three in ten did so.
translations.idiomatic: roads choked with refugees who robbed and killed one another; only two or three in ten reached home alive.

sentences.zh: 中原大亂。

translations.literal: The Central Plains fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 因以饑疫，人相食，無復耕者。

translations.literal: Famine and pestilence followed; men ate one another, and there were no longer any who plowed the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and plague followed; people ate the dead, and no one tilled the fields.

sentences.zh: 趙王祗使其將劉顯帥眾七萬攻鄴，軍於明光宮，去鄴二十三里。

translations.literal: Zhao King Zhi sent his general Liu Xian leading seventy thousand men to attack Ye, encamping at Mingguang Palace twenty-three li from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao king Zhi sent Liu Xian with seventy thousand men against Ye; they camped at Mingguang Palace, twenty-three li from the city.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔恐，召王泰，欲與之謀。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Min was afraid and summoned Wang Tai, wishing to consult with him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Min, alarmed, summoned Wang Tai to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 泰恚前言之不從，辭以瘡甚。

translations.literal: Tai resented that his earlier advice had not been followed and declined on the grounds that his sores were severe.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, still bitter that Min had ignored his counsel, pleaded severe sores.

sentences.zh: 閔親臨問之，泰固稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Min went in person to inquire; Tai still insisted his illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: Min visited him in person, but Tai insisted he was too ill.

sentences.zh: 閔怒，還宮，謂左右曰：「巴奴，乃公豈假汝為命邪！

translations.literal: Min was angry; returning to the palace he said to those around him, "Barbarian slave—does this old man need you to live!
translations.idiomatic: Min stormed back to the palace and told his attendants, "That barbarian wretch—do you think I need him to survive?

sentences.zh: 要將先滅群胡，卻斬王泰。

translations.literal: I intend first to destroy the Hu hordes, then behead Wang Tai."
translations.idiomatic: I'll wipe out the Hu first, then cut off Wang Tai's head."

sentences.zh: 」乃悉眾出戰，大破顯軍，追奔至陽平，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led out his entire force to battle, routed Xian's army utterly, pursued the fugitives to Yangping, and took more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out with his full army, crushed Liu Xian, pursued the fugitives to Yangping, and took more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 顯懼，密使請降，求殺祗以自效，閔乃引歸。

translations.literal: Xian was afraid and secretly sent to request surrender, offering to kill Zhi to prove his loyalty; Min then led him back.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xian secretly offered to surrender if he might kill Zhi to prove his loyalty; Min brought him back into service.

sentences.zh: 會有告王泰欲叛入秦者，閔殺之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Just then someone reported that Wang Tai intended to rebel and go over to Qin; Min killed him and exterminated his clan to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Wang Tai meant to defect to Qin. Min executed him and wiped out three generations of his family.

sentences.zh: 秦王健分遣使者問民疾苦，搜羅俊異，寬重斂之稅，弛離宮之禁，罷無用之器，去侈靡之服，凡趙之苛政不便於民者皆除之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian of Qin sent envoys in separate directions to inquire into the people's hardships, to seek out outstanding talent, to lighten heavy taxes, to relax prohibitions on detached palaces, to abolish useless implements, to remove extravagant garments, and to eliminate all harsh Zhao policies that harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Jian sent envoys across his realm to hear the people's grievances, recruit talent, cut heavy taxes, open the pleasure palaces, scrap useless regalia, ban lavish dress, and repeal every harsh Zhao law that burdened the common people.

sentences.zh: 杜洪、張琚遣使召梁州刺史司馬勳。

translations.literal: Du Hong and Zhang Ju sent envoys to summon Sima Xun, Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong and Zhang Ju sent envoys summoning Liang inspector Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，勳帥步騎三萬赴之，秦王健禦之於五丈原。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Xun led thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to answer them; Fu Jian of Qin met him at Wuzhang Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Xun marched thirty thousand foot and horse to their aid; Qin ruler Jian met him at Wuzhang Plains.

sentences.zh: 勳屢戰皆敗，退歸南鄭。

translations.literal: Xun fought repeatedly and was defeated each time, then withdrew to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun lost battle after battle and retreated to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 健以中書令賈玄碩始者不上尊號，銜之，使人告玄碩與司馬勳通，並其諸子皆殺之。

translations.literal: Jian bore a grudge because Director of the Imperial Secretariat Jia Xuanshuo had at first not submitted the exalted title; he had someone accuse Xuanshuo of communicating with Sima Xun, and killed him together with all his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Jian still resented Jia Xuanshuo for hesitating to press the royal title upon him. He fabricated a charge that Xuanshuo had conspired with Sima Xun and executed him along with all his sons.

sentences.zh: 渤海人逄約因趙亂，擁眾數千家附於魏，魏以約為渤海太守。

translations.literal: Peng Yue of Bohai, taking advantage of the chaos in Zhao, gathered several thousand households and submitted to Wei; Wei appointed Yue Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yue of Bohai, exploiting Zhao's collapse, rallied several thousand households and submitted to Wei, which made him administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 故太守劉准，隗之兄子也，土豪封放，弈之從弟也；

translations.literal: The former Administrator Liu Zhun was a nephew of Kou's elder brother; the local magnate Feng Fang was a cousin of Yi's.
translations.idiomatic: The former administrator Liu Zhun was a nephew of Kou Yi; the local strongman Feng Fang was a cousin of Yi.

sentences.zh: 別聚眾自守。

translations.literal: They gathered followers separately and held their own ground.
translations.idiomatic: Each gathered his own followers and held out on his own.

sentences.zh: 閔以准為幽州刺史，與約中分渤海。

translations.literal: Min appointed Zhun Inspector of You Province and divided Bohai between him and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Min made Zhun inspector of You and split Bohai between him and Yue.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊使封弈討約，使昌黎太守高開討准、放。

translations.literal: Murong Jun of Yan sent Feng Yi to attack Yue and Changli Administrator Gao Kai to attack Zhun and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Jun sent Feng Yi against Yue and Changli prefect Gao Kai against Zhun and Fang.

sentences.zh: 開，瞻之子也。

translations.literal: Kai was the son of Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was Zhan's son.

sentences.zh: 弈引兵直抵約壘，遣人謂約曰：「相與鄉里，隔絕日久，會遇甚難。

translations.literal: Yi led his troops straight to Yue's camp and sent someone to say to Yue, "We are fellow townsmen; separated a long time, it is hard to meet again.
translations.idiomatic: Yi marched straight to Yue's fort and sent word: "We are men of the same home country, long parted—this meeting is rare.

sentences.zh: 時事利害，人各有心，非所論也。

translations.literal: The gains and losses of the times—each man has his own mind; that is not what we should discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The rights and wrongs of the day are not what we need to argue about—each man has his own view.

sentences.zh: 願單出一相見，以寫佇結之情。

translations.literal: I wish to come out alone and meet you once, to release the feelings long pent up.
translations.idiomatic: Let us meet alone, just the two of us, to speak what has been on our hearts.

sentences.zh: 」約素信重弈，即出，見弈於門外。

translations.literal: Yue had always trusted and esteemed Yi, and at once went out and met Yi outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had always trusted Yi deeply, so he went out at once and met him outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 各屏騎卒，單馬交語。

translations.literal: Each dismissed his horsemen and spoke horse to horse alone.
translations.idiomatic: They sent away their escorts and spoke alone, each on his own horse.

sentences.zh: 弈與論敘平生畢，因說之曰：「與君累世同鄉，情相愛重，誠欲君享祚無窮；

translations.literal: When Yi had finished recounting their lives together, he then said to him, "With you I share hometown ties for generations; our affection is deep, and I truly wish you endless fortune;
translations.idiomatic: After they had reminisced about old times, Yi said, "We have been townsmen for generations and I hold you dear—I truly wish you lasting prosperity;

sentences.zh: 今既獲展奉，不可不盡所懷。

translations.literal: now that we have this meeting, I cannot but speak my whole mind.
translations.idiomatic: now that we can speak face to face, I must tell you everything on my mind.

sentences.zh: 冉閔乘石氏之亂，奄有成資，是宜天下服其強矣，而禍亂方始，固知天命不可力爭也。

translations.literal: Ran Min seized on the chaos of the Shi clan and suddenly gained the resources for success; the world ought to bow to his strength, yet calamity is only beginning—you surely know that the Mandate of Heaven cannot be wrested by force.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min rode the Shi family's collapse to sudden power, and for a time the realm seemed to bow to his might—but disaster is only starting. You must see that Heaven's mandate cannot be seized by force.

sentences.zh: 燕王弈也載德，奉義討亂，所征無敵。

translations.literal: The Yan king Jun bears virtue, upholds righteousness in punishing disorder, and in every campaign he is unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king Jun is virtuous, campaigns in the name of justice, and has never known defeat.

sentences.zh: 今已都薊，南臨趙、魏，遠近之民，襁負歸之。

translations.literal: He has now made his capital at Ji, faces south upon Zhao and Wei, and people near and far come to him carrying infants on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: He has established his capital at Ji, looks south over Zhao and Wei, and people flock to him from every quarter, infants strapped to their backs.

sentences.zh: 民厭荼毒，咸思有道。

translations.literal: The people are weary of bitter oppression and all long for a true way.
translations.idiomatic: The people are sick of tyranny and yearn for a righteous ruler.

sentences.zh: 冉閔之亡，匪朝伊夕，成敗之形，昭然易見。

translations.literal: Ran Min's fall is not a matter of many mornings or evenings—the shape of victory and defeat is plain for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min's downfall is only a matter of time—the outcome is already clear.

sentences.zh: 且燕王肇開王業，虛心賢俊，君能翻然改圖，則功參絳、灌，慶流苗裔，孰與為亡國將，守孤城以待必至之禍哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the Yan king has begun a royal enterprise and humbly welcomes the worthy; if you can turn about and change your course, your merit will rival Zhou Bo and Guan Ying, blessings will flow to your descendants—how does that compare with being a doomed general holding a lone city awaiting inevitable ruin!
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king is founding a dynasty and welcomes talent. If you change course now, your deeds may rival the founders of Han, and your line will prosper—why play the doomed general defending a lost city?

sentences.zh: 」約聞之，悵然不言。

translations.literal: When Yue heard this he was sorrowful and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue listened in silence, his face full of regret.

sentences.zh: 弈給使張安，有勇力；

translations.literal: Yi's attendant Zhang An was brave and strong;
translations.idiomatic: Yi's attendant Zhang An was a man of great strength;

sentences.zh: 弈豫戒之，俟約氣下，安突前持其馬鞚，因挾之而馳。

translations.literal: Yi had warned him beforehand; when Yue's spirit had subsided, An suddenly rushed forward, seized his bridle, and bore him off at a gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had instructed him in advance. When Yue's guard was down, An seized his bridle, pulled him onto his horse, and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 至營，弈與坐，謂曰：「君計不能自決，故相為決之，非欲取君以邀功，乃欲全君以安民也。

translations.literal: At the camp Yi sat with him and said, "You could not decide for yourself, so I decided for you—not to take you for merit, but to preserve you and settle the people."
translations.idiomatic: Back at camp Yi sat with him and said, "You could not choose for yourself, so I chose for you—not to win glory, but to save you and spare the people."

sentences.zh: 高開至渤海，准、放迎降。

translations.literal: When Gao Kai reached Bohai, Zhun and Fang came out to welcome him and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kai reached Bohai; Zhun and Fang came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 俊以放為渤海太守，准為左司馬，約參軍事。

translations.literal: Jun appointed Fang Administrator of Bohai, Zhun Left Major, and Yue a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Fang administrator of Bohai, Zhun his left major, and Yue a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 以約誘於人而遇獲，更其名曰釣。

translations.literal: Because Yue had been lured and captured, his name was changed to Diao.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue had been tricked and seized, they renamed him Diao.

sentences.zh: 劉顯弒趙王祗及其丞相安樂王炳、太宰趙庶等十餘人，傳首於鄴。

translations.literal: Liu Xian murdered Zhao King Zhi and his Chancellor the Prince of Anle, Bing, Grand Mentor Zhao Shu, and more than ten others, and sent their heads to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian assassinated Zhao king Zhi, Chancellor Prince of Anle Bing, Grand Mentor Zhao Shu, and more than ten others, and sent their heads to Ye.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍石寧奔柏人。

translations.literal: Flying Cavalry General Shi Ning fled to Boren.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Cavalry General Shi Ning fled to Boren.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔焚祗首於通衢，拜顯上大將軍、大單于、冀州牧。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Min burned Zhi's head in the public thoroughfare and appointed Xian Grand General, Great Chanyu, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruler Min burned Zhi's head in the open street and made Xian grand general, great chanyu, and governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 五月，趙兗州刺史劉啟自鄄城來奔。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Liu Qi, Inspector of Yan Province in Zhao, came over from Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Zhao's Yan inspector Liu Qi defected from Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，劉顯復引兵攻鄴，魏主閔擊敗之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Xian again led troops to attack Ye; the Wei ruler Min defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Xian attacked Ye again; Wei ruler Min beat him back.

sentences.zh: 顯還，稱帝於襄國。

translations.literal: Xian withdrew and declared himself emperor at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Xian withdrew and proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏徐州刺史周成、兗州刺史魏統、荊州刺史樂弘、豫州牧張遇以廩丘、許昌等諸城來降；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhou Cheng, Inspector of Xu Province in Wei, Wei Tong, Inspector of Yan Province, Yue Hong, Inspector of Jing Province, and Zhang Yu, Governor of Yu Province, surrendered the cities of Linqiu, Xuchang, and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wei's inspectors Zhou Cheng of Xu, Wei Tong of Yan, and Yue Hong of Jing, and Yu governor Zhang Yu, surrendered Linqiu, Xuchang, and other cities;

sentences.zh: 平南將軍高崇、征虜將軍呂護執洛州刺史鄭系，以其地來降。

translations.literal: Pacification-of-the-South General Gao Chong and Campaign General Lü Hu seized Luo Province Inspector Zheng Xi and surrendered his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification general Gao Chong and campaign general Lü Hu seized Luo inspector Zheng Xi and surrendered his territory.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊遣慕容恪攻中山，慕容評攻王午於魯口，魏中山太守上谷侯龕閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Murong Jun of Yan sent Murong Ke to attack Zhongshan and Murong Ping to attack Wang Wu at Lukou; Wei Administrator of Zhongshan Hou Kan of Shanggu shut the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Murong Ke against Zhongshan and Murong Ping against Wang Wu at Lukou; Wei's Zhongshan prefect Hou Kan of Shanggu barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 恪南徇常山，軍於九門，魏趙郡太守遼西李邽舉郡降，恪厚撫之，將邽還圍中山，侯龕乃降。

translations.literal: Ke marched south through Changshan and encamped at Jiumen; Li Gui of Liaoxi, Administrator of Zhao Commandery in Wei, surrendered the whole commandery; Ke treated him generously, brought Gui back to besiege Zhongshan, and then Hou Kan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ke swept south through Changshan and camped at Jiumen. Li Gui of Liaoxi, Wei's Zhao prefect, surrendered his entire commandery. Ke treated him well, brought him back to besiege Zhongshan, and Hou Kan then submitted.

sentences.zh: 恪入中山，遷其將帥、土豪數十家詣薊，餘皆安堵；

translations.literal: Ke entered Zhongshan, moved several dozen families of its generals and local magnates to Ji, and the rest were left undisturbed;
translations.idiomatic: Ke entered Zhongshan, relocated dozens of leading families to Ji, and left the rest in peace;

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴明，秋豪不犯。

translations.literal: military discipline was strict and not a hair of the people was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: discipline was iron, and not even a blade of grass was taken from the people.

sentences.zh: 慕容評至南安，王午遣其將鄭生拒戰，抨擊斬之。

translations.literal: Murong Ping reached Nan'an; Wang Wu sent his general Zheng Sheng to resist; Ping attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping reached Nan'an. Wang Wu sent Zheng Sheng to fight; Ping struck and killed him.

sentences.zh: 悅綰還自襄國，俊乃知張舉之妄而殺之。

translations.literal: When Yue Chuo returned from Xiangguo, Jun then learned that Zhang Ju had lied and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Chuo returned from Xiangguo; Jun learned Zhang Ju had deceived him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 常煒有四男二女在中山，俊釋煒之囚，使諸子就見之。

translations.literal: Chang Wei had four sons and two daughters in Zhongshan; Jun released Wei from prison and had his children come to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Wei had four sons and two daughters in Zhongshan. Jun freed him and let his children visit.

sentences.zh: 煒上疏謝恩，俊手令答曰：「卿本不為生計，孤以州裡相存耳。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial thanking him for grace; Jun replied in his own hand, "You were never seeking a livelihood—I kept you for our shared homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Wei wrote to thank him. Jun replied in his own hand: "You were never scheming for gain—I held you only because we share a homeland.

sentences.zh: 今大亂之中，諸子盡至，豈非天所念邪！

translations.literal: Now in the midst of great disorder all your children have come—is this not Heaven's care!
translations.idiomatic: In this chaos all your children have found you—surely Heaven itself has taken pity!

sentences.zh: 天且念卿，況於孤乎！

translations.literal: If Heaven cares for you, how much more should I!
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven remembers you, how can I do less!

sentences.zh: 」賜妾一人，谷三百斛，使居凡城。

translations.literal: He granted one concubine, three hundred hu of grain, and had him dwell at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a concubine, three hundred hu of grain, and a home at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 以北平太守孫興為中山太守。

translations.literal: He appointed Sun Xing, Administrator of Beiping, Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Beiping prefect Sun Xing to govern Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 興善於綏撫，中山遂安。

translations.literal: Xing was skilled at soothing the people, and Zhongshan was thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xing governed with a gentle hand, and Zhongshan grew calm.

sentences.zh: 庫辱官偉帥部眾自上黨降燕。

translations.literal: Guan Wei of Kurong led his followers down from Shangdang to surrender to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wei of the Kurong tribe led his people down from Shangdang to submit to Yan.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲遣使來請降。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong sent envoys to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，以弋仲為使持節、六夷大都督、督江北諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大單于、高陵郡公，又以其子襄為持節、平北將軍、都督并州諸軍事、并州刺史、平鄉縣公。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Yizhong was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Commander of the Six Yi, Supervisor of All Military Affairs North of the River, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of an Office with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies, Great Chanyu, and Duke of Gaoling Commandery; his son Xiang was made Bearer of the Staff, Pacifier of the North General, Commander of All Military Affairs in Bing Province, Inspector of Bing Province, and Duke of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Yizhong received the staff of authority as grand commander of the six barbarian peoples, supervisor of all forces north of the Yangzi, general of chariots and cavalry, grand chanyu, and Duke of Gaoling; his son Xiang became pacifier of the north, commander of Bing forces, Bing inspector, and Duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 逄釣亡歸渤海，招集舊眾以叛燕。

translations.literal: Peng Diao fled back to Bohai, gathered his old followers, and rebelled against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Diao escaped to Bohai, rallied his old followers, and rebelled against Yan.

sentences.zh: 樂陵太守賈堅使人告諭鄉人，示以成敗，釣部眾稍散，遂來奔。

translations.literal: Jia Jian, Administrator of Leling, sent men to instruct his countrymen and show them success and failure; Diao's followers gradually dispersed, and he then came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Leling prefect Jia Jian sent men to warn the locals where fortune lay; Diao's followers drifted away, and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾葉延卒，子碎妥立。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Yeyan died and his son Sui Tuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun chief Yeyan died; his son Sui Tuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 初，桓溫聞石氏亂，上疏請出師經略另原，事久不報。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huan Wen heard of disorder in the Shi clan, he submitted a memorial requesting to lead an expedition to recover the Central Plains; for a long time there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, hearing of the Shi family's collapse, Huan Wen had asked permission to march north and recover the Central Plains, but the court never answered.

sentences.zh: 溫知朝廷仗殷浩以抗己，甚忿之；

translations.literal: Wen knew the court relied on Yin Hao to oppose him and was greatly resentful;
translations.idiomatic: Wen knew the court was using Yin Hao to check him and burned with resentment;

sentences.zh: 然素知浩之為人，亦不之憚也。

translations.literal: yet he had always known Hao's character and did not fear him either.
translations.idiomatic: yet he had always known Hao's character and did not truly fear him.

sentences.zh: 以國無他釁，遂得相持彌年，雖有君臣之跡，羈縻而已，八州士眾資調殆不為國家用。

translations.literal: Because the state had no other troubles, they were able to stalemate for years; though the forms of ruler and subject remained, it was only nominal restraint, and the levies of the eight provinces scarcely served the court.
translations.idiomatic: With no other crisis at hand, the standoff dragged on for years. Ruler and subject kept up appearances, but it was restraint in name only—the eight provinces' taxes barely reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 屢求北伐，詔書不聽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sought a northern campaign, but imperial edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again and again to march north, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛未，溫拜表輒行，帥眾四五萬順流而下，軍於武昌，朝廷大懼。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinwei, Wen memorialized and marched without waiting, leading forty or fifty thousand men downstream; he encamped at Wuchang, and the court was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinwei, Wen submitted his memorial and marched anyway with forty or fifty thousand men down the Yangzi, halting at Wuchang. The court was terrified.

sentences.zh: 殷浩欲去位以避溫，又欲以騶虞幡駐溫軍。

translations.literal: Yin Hao wished to leave office to avoid Wen and also wished to use the zouyu banner to halt Wen's army.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao wanted to resign to escape Wen and even proposed stopping his army with the imperial zouyu banner.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王彪之言於會稽王昱曰：「此屬皆自為計，非能保社稷，為殿下計也。

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said to the Prince of Kuaiji, Yu, "These men are all scheming for themselves; they cannot preserve the altars of state—they are not planning for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel director Wang Biaozhi told Prince of Kuaiji Yu, "These men are looking out for themselves, not the realm—they are not thinking of you.

sentences.zh: 若殷浩去職，人情離駭，天子獨坐，當此之際，必有任其責者，非殿下而誰乎！

translations.literal: If Yin Hao leaves his post, the people's hearts will scatter in alarm; the Son of Heaven sits alone—at such a moment someone must bear the responsibility, and who if not Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: If Yin Hao steps down, the court will panic and the emperor will stand alone. Someone must answer for the realm then—and who but you?

sentences.zh: 」又謂浩曰：「彼若抗表問罪，卿為之首。

translations.literal: He also said to Hao, "If he submits a memorial accusing you, you will be the first named.
translations.idiomatic: He told Hao as well, "If Wen denounces you in a memorial, you will be named first.

sentences.zh: 事任如此，猜釁已成，欲作匹夫，豈有全地邪！

translations.literal: Matters have come to this; suspicion and breach are already formed—if you wish to become a common man, can you keep your body whole!
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion is already fixed. If you try to become a private citizen now, do you think you will survive?

sentences.zh: 且當靜以待之。

translations.literal: For now you should wait calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Stay calm and wait.

sentences.zh: 令相王與手書，示以款誠，為陳成敗，彼必旋師；

translations.literal: Have the Prince Regent write in his own hand, show sincerity, explain success and failure—he will surely turn his army back;
translations.idiomatic: Have the prince regent write in his own hand, speak sincerely, and explain how this will end—Wen will turn back;

sentences.zh: 若不從，則遣中詔；

translations.literal: if he does not obey, then send an imperial edict from within;
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses, send an imperial edict;

sentences.zh: 又不從，乃當以正義相裁。

translations.literal: if he still does not obey, then you must judge him by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: if he still refuses, then act in the name of justice.

sentences.zh: 奈何無故匆匆，先自猖獗乎！

translations.literal: Why rush about for no reason and run wild first yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Why panic and make the first reckless move!

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「決大事正自難，頃日來欲使人悶。

translations.literal: Hao said, "Deciding great affairs is indeed difficult; these last days have been stifling.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Great decisions are never easy. These last days have been suffocating.

sentences.zh: 聞卿此謀，意始得了。

translations.literal: Hearing your plan, my mind is at last relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing your counsel, I can breathe again."

sentences.zh: 」彪之，彬之子也。

translations.literal: Biaozhi was the son of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi was the son of Wang Bin.

sentences.zh: 撫軍司馬高崧言於昱曰：「王宜致書，諭以禍福，自當返旆。

translations.literal: Gao Song, Major of the Pacification Army, said to Yu, "Your Highness should send a letter explaining fortune and disaster—he will turn his banners back of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Army major Gao Song told Yu, "You should write to him, explain the stakes, and he will withdraw of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，便六軍整駕，逆順於茲判矣！

translations.literal: If not, then the six armies will array their chariots—loyalty and rebellion will be decided here!"
translations.idiomatic: If not, the six armies will march—and loyalty and treason will be decided on the spot!"

sentences.zh: 」乃於坐為昱草書曰：「寇難宜平，時會宜接。

translations.literal: Thereupon, still seated, he drafted a letter for Yu: "Bandit troubles should be pacified; the season should be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he drafted a letter for Yu on the spot: "The enemy must be subdued; the moment must be seized.

sentences.zh: 此實為國遠圖，經略大算，能弘斯會，非足下而誰？

translations.literal: This is truly the long-range plan for the state, the great design of strategy—who but you can fulfill this opportunity?
translations.idiomatic: This is the great design of statecraft—who but you can rise to such a moment?

sentences.zh: 但以比興師動眾，要當以資實為本；

translations.literal: Only in raising armies at this time, supplies and strength must be the foundation;
translations.idiomatic: But any campaign must rest on real resources;

sentences.zh: 運轉之艱，古人所難，不可易之於始而不熟慮。

translations.literal: the hardship of transport was difficult even for the ancients—it cannot be treated lightly at the outset without thorough consideration.
translations.idiomatic: logistics defeated armies even in antiquity—you cannot treat that lightly at the start.

sentences.zh: 頃所以深用為疑，惟在此耳。

translations.literal: The reason for my deep doubts lately is solely this.
translations.idiomatic: That alone is why I have hesitated.

sentences.zh: 然異常之舉，眾之所駭，游聲噂□沓，想足下亦少聞之。

translations.literal: Yet an extraordinary move alarms the multitude; wandering rumors buzz and swarm—you too have surely heard a little of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet an extraordinary move alarms everyone; rumors are already swirling—you must have heard them.

sentences.zh: 苟患失之，無所不至，或能望風振擾，一時崩散。

translations.literal: If men fear losing what they have, they will go to any length; perhaps at the mere rumor they will stir and scatter in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Men who fear losing what they have will do anything; at the first rumor your army may melt away.

sentences.zh: 如此則望實並喪，社稷之事去矣。

translations.literal: If so, reputation and substance will both be lost, and the affairs of the altars of state will be gone.
translations.idiomatic: Then your name and your cause are both lost, and the realm with them.

sentences.zh: 皆由吾闇弱，德信不著，不能鎮靜群庶，保固維城，所以內愧於心，外慚良友。

translations.literal: All this is because I am dim and weak, my virtue and trust not manifest, unable to calm the masses and secure the bulwarks—therefore I am ashamed within and blush before good friends without.
translations.idiomatic: All this is because I am weak and my authority uncertain, unable to steady the people and hold the realm together—I am ashamed before you and before my own conscience.

sentences.zh: 吾與足下，雖職有內外，安社稷，保家國，其致一也。

translations.literal: You and I, though our offices divide inner and outer, in securing the altars of state and preserving family and realm, our aim is one.
translations.idiomatic: You and I serve in different posts, but in securing the realm our aim is the same.

sentences.zh: 天下安危，系之明德。

translations.literal: The safety or peril of the realm hangs upon your bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the empire rests on your judgment.

sentences.zh: 當先思寧國而後圖其外，使王基克隆，大義弘著，所望於足下。

translations.literal: You should first think of settling the state and afterward plan outward affairs, so that the royal foundation flourishes and great righteousness is displayed—this is what I hope from you.
translations.idiomatic: Settle the realm first, then look outward—let the dynasty flourish and righteousness prevail. That is what I ask of you.

sentences.zh: 區區誠懷，豈可復顧嫌而不盡哉！

translations.literal: This humble sincere heart—how can I still consider scruples and not speak fully!
translations.idiomatic: I speak from the heart—how can I hold anything back!

sentences.zh: 」溫即上疏惶恐致謝，回軍還鎮。

translations.literal: Wen at once submitted a memorial in fear and thanks, turned his army about, and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Wen immediately submitted a humble memorial of thanks, turned his army around, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將行郊祀。

translations.literal: The court was about to perform the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The court prepared to perform the suburban sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱問於王彪之曰：「郊祀應有赦否？

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Yu, asked Wang Biaozhi, "Should there be an amnesty at the suburban sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Kuaiji Yu asked Wang Biaozhi, "Should we proclaim an amnesty with the suburban rites?

sentences.zh: 」彪之曰：「自中興以來，郊祀往往有赦，愚意常謂非宜；

translations.literal: Biaozhi said, "Since the Restoration, suburban sacrifices have often been accompanied by amnesties, but in my humble view this is not fitting;
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi answered, "Since the Restoration, amnesties have often followed the suburban rites, but I have always thought that unwise;

sentences.zh: 凶愚之人，以為郊必有赦，將生心於徼幸矣！

translations.literal: vicious and foolish men, thinking that a suburban sacrifice always brings amnesty, will set their hearts on lucky chances!"
translations.idiomatic: wicked and foolish men will count on it and scheme for clemency!"

sentences.zh: 」昱從之。

translations.literal: Yu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took his advice.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊如龍城。

translations.literal: Murong Jun of Yan went to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Jun traveled to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 丁零翟鼠帥所部降燕，封為歸義王。

translations.literal: Zhai Shu of the Dingling led his followers to surrender to Yan and was enfeoffed as Prince Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Shu of the Dingling submitted with his followers and was created Prince Who Returns to Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinmao, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: That spring, in the first month on the day xinmao, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄等請秦王健正尊號，依漢、晉之舊，不必效石氏之初。

translations.literal: Fu Xiong, Chancellor of Qin, and others asked Fu Jian of Qin to rectify his exalted title, following the precedents of Han and Jin, without need to imitate the Shi clan's early ways.
translations.idiomatic: Qin chancellor Fu Xiong and others urged Jian to take the full imperial title in the manner of Han and Jin, not the Shi family's early pretensions.

sentences.zh: 健從之，即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: Jian complied, assumed the imperial throne, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian agreed, ascended the imperial throne, and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 諸公皆進爵為王。

translations.literal: All the dukes were advanced in rank to kings.
translations.idiomatic: All the princes were promoted to kings.

sentences.zh: 且言單于所以統壹百蠻，非天子所宜領，以授太子萇。

translations.literal: They also said that the Chanyu title, by which the hundred barbarians are unified, was not fitting for the Son of Heaven to hold, and it was conferred on the Crown Prince Chang.
translations.idiomatic: They also said the title of chanyu, which unites the barbarian peoples, was not for the emperor to bear, and gave it to crown prince Chang.

sentences.zh: 司馬勳既還漢中，杜洪、張琚屯宜秋。

translations.literal: After Sima Xun had returned to Hanzhong, Du Hong and Zhang Ju encamped at Yiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Xun withdrew to Hanzhong, Du Hong and Zhang Ju camped at Yiqiu.

sentences.zh: 洪自以右族，輕琚，琚遂殺洪，自立為秦王，改元建昌。

translations.literal: Hong considered himself of a great clan and looked down on Ju; Ju then killed Hong, declared himself King of Qin, and changed the era name to Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, proud of his eminent lineage, despised Ju, who killed him, declared himself King of Qin, and adopted the era name Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 劉顯攻常山，魏主閔留大將軍蔣干使輔太子智守鄴，自將八千騎救之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian attacked Changshan; the Wei ruler Min left Grand General Jiang Gan to assist Crown Prince Zhi in defending Ye and personally led eight thousand horsemen to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian attacked Changshan. Min left Grand General Jiang Gan to help Crown Prince Zhi hold Ye and rode out with eight thousand cavalry to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 顯大司馬清河王寧以棗強降魏。

translations.literal: Xian's Grand Marshal, the Prince of Qinghe, Ning, surrendered Zaoqiang to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's grand marshal, Prince of Qinghe Ning, surrendered Zaoqiang to Wei.

sentences.zh: 閔擊顯，敗之，追奔至襄國。

translations.literal: Min attacked Xian, defeated him, and pursued the fugitives to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Min routed Xian and pursued the fugitives to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 顯大將軍曹伏駒開門納閔。

translations.literal: Xian's Grand General Cao Fuju opened the gates and admitted Min.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's general Cao Fuju opened the gates to Min.

sentences.zh: 閔殺顯及其公卿己下百餘人，焚襄國宮室，遷其民於鄴。

translations.literal: Min killed Xian and more than a hundred of his ministers and officials, burned the palaces of Xiangguo, and moved its people to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Min executed Xian and more than a hundred of his officials, burned Xiangguo's palaces, and relocated its people to Ye.

sentences.zh: 趙汝陰王琨以其妻妾來奔，斬於建康市，石氏遂絕。

translations.literal: The Zhao Prince of Ruyin, Kun, came over with his wives and concubines; he was beheaded in the market at Jiankang, and the house of Shi was thereby extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's Prince of Ruyin Kun fled with his household; he was beheaded in Jiankang's market, and the house of Shi came to an end.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞孔嚴言於殷浩曰：「比來眾情，良可寒心，不知使君當何以鎮之。

translations.literal: Kong Yan, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, said to Yin Hao, "Lately the mood of the masses is truly chilling—one wonders how you, my lord, will steady it.
translations.idiomatic: Left secretariat assistant Kong Yan told Yin Hao, "Public feeling lately is alarming. How will you steady it?

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜明受任之方，韓、彭專征伐，蕭、曹守管籥，內外之任，各有攸司；

translations.literal: In my humble view you should clarify the division of duties: Han Xin and Peng Yue devoted themselves to campaigns, Xiao He and Cao Shen guarded the keys—inner and outer tasks each have their office;
translations.idiomatic: You should clarify roles: let Huan Wen fight as Han Xin did, while you hold the capital as Xiao He did—each man to his charge;

sentences.zh: 深思廉、藺屈身之義，平、勃交歡之謀，令穆然無間，然後可以保大定功也。

translations.literal: ponder deeply the meaning of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru yielding to one another, and the counsel of Chen Ping and Zhou Bo in joining in friendship, so that all is serene without rift—only then can you preserve the great enterprise and settle achievement.
translations.idiomatic: remember how Lian Po and Lin Xiangru swallowed pride for the realm, how Chen Ping and Zhou Bo made peace—only then can you secure great deeds.

sentences.zh: 觀頃日降附之徒，皆人面獸心，貪而無親，恐難以義感也。

translations.literal: Looking at those who have lately surrendered, all have human faces and beast hearts, greedy and without loyalty—I fear they will be hard to move by righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The men who have lately submitted have human faces and beasts' hearts—greedy and faithless. Righteousness will not move them."

sentences.zh: 」浩不從。

translations.literal: Hao did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 嚴，愉之從子也。

translations.literal: Yan was a nephew of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a nephew of Yu.

sentences.zh: 浩上疏請北出許、洛，詔許之。

translations.literal: Hao submitted a memorial requesting to advance north to Xu and Luo; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao memorialized to march north toward Xu and Luoyang; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 以安西將軍謝尚、北中郎獎荀羨為督統，進屯壽春。

translations.literal: Anxi General Xie Shang and Northern Gentlemen-of-the-House Xun Xian were made overall commanders and advanced to encamp at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi general Xie Shang and Northern Gentlemen Xun Xian were placed in overall command and advanced to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 謝尚不能撫尉張遇，遇怒，據許昌叛，使其將上官恩據洛陽，樂弘攻督護戴施於倉垣，浩軍不能進。

translations.literal: Xie Shang could not soothe Zhang Yu; Yu was angry, seized Xuchang in rebellion, sent his general Shangguan En to hold Luoyang, and Yue Hong attacked Supervisor Dai Shi at Cangyuan—Hao's army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang failed to win over Zhang Yu, who seized Xuchang in revolt, sent Shangguan En to hold Luoyang, and had Yue Hong attack Dai Shi at Cangyuan. Hao's army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 三月，命荀羨鎮准陰，尋加監青州諸軍事，又領兗州刺史，鎮下邳。

translations.literal: In the third month he ordered Xun Xian to garrison Huaiyin; soon after he was additionally made overseer of all military affairs in Qing Province, and also held the post of Inspector of Yan Province, garrisoning Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xun Xian was posted to Huaiyin, then made overseer of Qing forces and Yan inspector, with his base at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，燕王俊還薊，稍徙軍中文武兵民家屬於薊。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Murong Jun of Yan returned to Ji and gradually moved the civil and military personnel and civilian families of the army to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Yan ruler Jun returned to Ji and gradually relocated army families there.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲有子四十二人，及病，謂諸子曰：「石氏待吾厚，吾本欲為之盡力。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong had forty-two sons; when he fell ill he told his sons, "The Shi clan treated me generously; I originally meant to serve them with all my strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong had forty-two sons. On his deathbed he told them, "The Shi treated me well, and I meant to serve them faithfully.

sentences.zh: 今石氏已滅，中原無主；

translations.literal: Now the Shi are destroyed and the Central Plains have no master;
translations.idiomatic: Now the Shi are gone and the heartland has no lord;

sentences.zh: 我死，汝亟自歸於晉，當固執臣節，無為不義也！

translations.literal: when I die, you must quickly submit to Jin yourselves, hold fast to the duty of subjects, and do nothing unrighteous!"
translations.idiomatic: when I die, submit to Jin at once, keep faith as subjects, and do no wrong!"

sentences.zh: 」弋仲卒，子襄秘不發喪，帥戶六萬南攻陽平、元城、發乾，破之，屯於碻磝津，以太原王亮為長史，天水尹赤為司馬，太原薛瓚、略陽權翼為參軍。

translations.literal: When Yizhong died, his son Xiang kept the death secret, led sixty thousand households south to attack Yangping, Yuancheng, and Fagan, defeated them, and encamped at Que'ao Ford; he made Wang Liang of Taiyuan Chief Clerk, Yin Chi of Tianshui Major, and Xue Zan of Taiyuan and Quan Yi of Lueyang staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong died. Xiang hid the death, led sixty thousand households south against Yangping, Yuancheng, and Fagan, took them, and camped at Que'ao Ford. He appointed Wang Liang chief clerk, Yin Chi major, and Xue Zan and Quan Yi as staff officers.

sentences.zh: 襄與秦兵戰，敗，亡三萬餘戶，南至滎陽，始發喪。

translations.literal: Xiang fought Qin troops, was defeated, lost more than thirty thousand households, reached Xingyang in the south, and only then announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang fought the Qin army, lost, shed more than thirty thousand households, reached Xingyang, and only then announced his father's death.

sentences.zh: 又與秦將高昌、李歷戰於麻田，馬中流矢而斃。

translations.literal: He again fought Qin generals Gao Chang and Li Li at Matian; his horse was struck by a stray arrow and fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: At Matian he fought Qin generals Gao Chang and Li Li; a stray arrow killed his horse.

sentences.zh: 弟萇以馬授襄，襄曰：「汝何以自免？

translations.literal: His younger brother Chang gave Xiang his horse; Xiang said, "How will you save yourself?
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chang gave him his horse. Xiang said, "How will you escape?

sentences.zh: 」萇曰：「但令兄濟，豎子必不敢害萇！

translations.literal: Chang said, "Only let elder brother get across—the brats will not dare harm Chang!"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Once you are safe, those wretches will not dare touch me!"

sentences.zh: 」會救至，俱免。

translations.literal: Rescue arrived, and both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue arrived and both escaped.

sentences.zh: 尹赤奔秦，秦以赤為并州刺史，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Yin Chi fled to Qin; Qin made Chi Inspector of Bing Province, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chi defected to Qin, which made him Bing inspector at Puban.

sentences.zh: 襄遂帥眾歸晉，送其五弟為質。

translations.literal: Xiang then led his followers to submit to Jin and sent five younger brothers as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then submitted to Jin with his followers and sent five younger brothers as hostages.

sentences.zh: 詔襄屯譙城，襄單騎渡淮，見謝尚於壽春。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xiang to garrison Qiaocheng; Xiang crossed the Huai alone on horseback and met Xie Shang at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xiang to Qiaocheng. He crossed the Huai alone and met Xie Shang at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 尚聞其名，命去仗衛，幅巾待之，歡若平生。

translations.literal: Shang had heard his reputation and ordered away arms and guards, received him in plain headcloth, and rejoiced with him as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Shang, knowing his fame, dismissed guards, received him informally, and welcomed him like an old friend.

sentences.zh: 襄博學，善談論，江東人士皆重之。

translations.literal: Xiang was learned and skilled in discourse; the gentlemen east of the river all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was learned and eloquent, and men of the southeast held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔既克襄國，因游食常山、中山諸郡。

translations.literal: After the Wei ruler Min had taken Xiangguo, he foraged through the commanderies of Changshan and Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Xiangguo, Wei ruler Min foraged through Changshan and Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 趙立義將軍段勤聚胡、羯萬餘人保據繹幕，自稱趙帝。

translations.literal: Duan Qin, Establishing Righteousness General of Zhao, gathered more than ten thousand Hu and Jie and held Yimu, styling himself Emperor of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao general Duan Qin rallied more than ten thousand Hu and Jie at Yimu and proclaimed himself Zhao emperor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，燕王俊遣慕容恪擊魏，慕容霸等擊勤。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiazi, Murong Jun of Yan sent Murong Ke to attack Wei and Murong Ba and others to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiazi, Yan ruler Jun sent Murong Ke against Wei and Murong Ba against Qin.

sentences.zh: 魏主閔將與燕戰，大將軍董閏、車騎將軍張溫諫曰：「鮮卑乘勝鋒銳，且彼眾我寡，請且避之，俟其驕惰，然後益兵以擊之，」閔怒曰：「吾欲以此眾平幽州，斬慕容俊；

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Min was about to fight Yan; Grand General Dong Run and General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Wen remonstrated, "The Xianbei ride their victory with sharp momentum, and they are many while we are few—please avoid them for now, wait until they grow arrogant and slack, then add troops and strike." Min said angrily, "I mean to pacify You Province with this host and behead Murong Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Min prepared to fight Yan. Grand General Dong Run and Cavalry General Zhang Wen urged caution: "The Xianbei are fresh from victory and outnumber us—withdraw until they grow careless, then strike." Min raged, "With this army I will pacify Youzhou and take Murong Jun's head;

sentences.zh: 今遇恪而避之，人謂我何！

translations.literal: now that I meet Ke and shrink back—what will men say of me!
translations.idiomatic: and now you want me to flee from Ke—what will men say!

sentences.zh: 」司徒劉茂、特進郎闓相謂曰：「吾君此行，必不還矣，吾等何為坐待戮辱！

translations.literal: Minister of Education Liu Mao and Special Advance Lang Kan said to each other, "Our lord on this expedition will surely not return—why should we sit and await slaughter and disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Mao and Lang Kan whispered to each other, "Our lord will not return from this march—why sit here waiting to be killed?

sentences.zh: 」皆自殺。

translations.literal: Both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 閔軍於安喜，慕容恪引兵從之。

translations.literal: Min encamped at Anxi; Murong Ke led his troops after him.
translations.idiomatic: Min camped at Anxi; Murong Ke followed.

sentences.zh: 閔趣常山，恪追之，丙子，及於魏昌之廉臺。

translations.literal: Min hastened toward Changshan; Ke pursued, and on the day bingzi overtook him at Liantai in Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: Min hurried toward Changshan; Ke caught him on the day bingzi at Liantai in Weichang.

sentences.zh: 閔與燕兵十戰，燕兵皆不勝。

translations.literal: Min fought the Yan army ten times; the Yan troops were victorious in none.
translations.idiomatic: Min fought ten engagements; the Yan army lost every one.

sentences.zh: 閔素有勇名，所將兵精銳，燕人憚之。

translations.literal: Min had long borne a name for valor; the troops he led were elite and sharp, and the Yan men feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Min was famed for courage and led elite troops; the Yan feared him.

sentences.zh: 慕容恪巡陳，謂將士曰：「冉閔勇而無謀，一夫敵耳！

translations.literal: Murong Ke inspected the battle line and told his officers and soldiers, "Ran Min is brave but without strategy—a match for a single man only!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke rode the lines and told his men, "Ran Min is brave but stupid—a single champion, nothing more!

sentences.zh: 其士卒饑疲，甲兵雖精，其實難用，不足破也！

translations.literal: His soldiers are hungry and weary; though their armor and weapons are fine, in truth they are hard to use—not enough to break us!"
translations.idiomatic: His men are hungry and exhausted. Fine arms cannot save them—we need not fear him!"

sentences.zh: 」閔以所將多步卒，而燕皆騎兵，引兵將趣林中。

translations.literal: Min, since those he led were mostly foot soldiers while Yan were all cavalry, was about to lead his troops toward the woods.
translations.idiomatic: Min's force was mostly infantry against Yan cavalry, so he headed for the woods.

sentences.zh: 恪參軍高開曰：「吾騎兵利平地，若閔得入林，不可復製。

translations.literal: Ke's staff officer Gao Kai said, "Our cavalry excel on open ground; if Min reaches the forest he cannot be controlled again.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's officer Gao Kai said, "Our cavalry need open ground. If Min reaches the trees we lose him.

sentences.zh: 宜亟遣輕騎邀之，既合而陽走，誘致平地，然後可擊也」。

translations.literal: We should quickly send light cavalry to intercept him; after joining battle feign retreat, lure him to level ground, and then we can strike."
translations.idiomatic: Send light horse to cut him off, feign retreat after contact, lure him onto the plain, then strike."

sentences.zh: 恪從之。

translations.literal: Ke followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Ke agreed.

sentences.zh: 魏兵還就平地，恪分軍為三部，謂諸將曰：「閔性輕銳，又自以眾少，必致死於我。

translations.literal: The Wei troops returned to open ground; Ke divided his army into three parts and told his generals, "Min is impetuous and sharp, and since he thinks himself few he will surely fight to the death against us.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army came back to open ground. Ke divided his force in three and told his generals, "Min is reckless and thinks himself outnumbered—he will fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 我厚集中軍之陳以待之，俟其合戰，卿等從旁擊之，無不克矣。

translations.literal: I shall mass the central army's formation thickly to await him; when he joins battle, you shall strike from the flanks—there is none we cannot overcome."
translations.idiomatic: I will mass the center and wait. When he engages, strike from the flanks—you cannot fail."

sentences.zh: 」乃擇鮮卑善射者五千人，以鐵鎖連其馬，為方陳而前。

translations.literal: He then chose five thousand Xianbei skilled in archery, linked their horses with iron chains, and advanced in a square formation.
translations.idiomatic: He chose five thousand Xianbei archers, chained their horses together, and advanced in a square formation.

sentences.zh: 閔所乘駿馬曰朱龍，日行千里。

translations.literal: The fine horse Min rode was called Vermilion Dragon and could travel a thousand li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: Min rode a stallion called Vermilion Dragon that could run a thousand li in a day.

sentences.zh: 閔左操雙刃矛，右執鉤戟，以擊燕兵，斬首三百餘級。

translations.literal: Min wielded a double-bladed spear in his left hand and a hook halberd in his right, struck the Yan troops, and took more than three hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: With a double-bladed spear in his left hand and a hook halberd in his right, he cut down more than three hundred Yan soldiers.

sentences.zh: 望見大幢，知其為中軍，直衝之；

translations.literal: Seeing the great banner and knowing it marked the central army, he charged straight at it;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the great banner of the center, he charged straight for it;

sentences.zh: 燕兩軍從旁夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: the two Yan wings struck from the sides and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: the two Yan wings struck from the flanks and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 圍閔數重，閔潰圍東走二十餘里，朱龍忽斃，為燕兵所執。

translations.literal: They surrounded Min in many rings; he broke out and fled east more than twenty li; Vermilion Dragon suddenly fell dead, and he was seized by Yan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded many times over, Min broke out and fled east more than twenty li until Vermilion Dragon dropped dead and Yan troops seized him.

sentences.zh: 燕人殺魏僕射劉群，執董閔、張溫，及閔皆送於薊。

translations.literal: The Yan killed Wei's Vice Director Liu Qun, seized Dong Run and Zhang Wen, and sent them together with Min to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan killed Wei's vice director Liu Qun, seized Dong Run and Zhang Wen, and sent them with Min to Ji.

sentences.zh: 閔子操奔魯口。

translations.literal: Min's son Cao fled to Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: Min's son Cao fled to Lukou.

sentences.zh: 高開被創而卒。

translations.literal: Gao Kai died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Kai died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 慕容恪進屯常山，俊命恪鎮中山。

translations.literal: Murong Ke advanced and encamped at Changshan; Jun ordered Ke to garrison Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke advanced to Changshan; Jun ordered him to hold Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 己卯，冉閔至薊。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Ran Min arrived at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, Ran Min was brought to Ji.

sentences.zh: 俊大赦，立閔而責之曰：「汝奴僕下才，何得妄稱帝？

translations.literal: Jun proclaimed a general amnesty, had Min stand before him, and rebuked him, saying, "You slave of low talent—how dare you presumptuously call yourself emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Jun proclaimed an amnesty, confronted Min, and demanded, "You base-born slave—how dare you call yourself emperor?

sentences.zh: 」閔曰：「天下大亂，爾曹夷狄禽獸之類猶稱帝，況我中土英雄，何為不得稱帝邪！

translations.literal: Min said, "The realm is in great disorder—even you barbarian birds and beasts call yourselves emperors; how much more may a hero of the Central Lands not be emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Min answered, "The realm is in chaos—even you barbarian beasts call yourselves emperors. Why should a hero of the Central Lands not do the same!

sentences.zh: 」俊怒，鞭之三百，送於龍城。

translations.literal: Jun was furious, had him flogged three hundred strokes, and sent him to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had him flogged three hundred times and sent him to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 慕容霸軍至繹幕，段勤與弟思陪舉城降。

translations.literal: Murong Ba's army reached Yimu; Duan Qin and his younger brother Sipei surrendered the whole city.
