translations.idiomatic: Murong Ba reached Yimu; Duan Qin and his brother Sipei surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 甲申，俊遣慕容評及中尉侯龕帥精騎萬人攻鄴。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Jun sent Murong Ping and Central Commandant Hou Kan leading ten thousand elite horsemen to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Jun sent Murong Ping and Hou Kan with ten thousand elite cavalry against Ye.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，至鄴，魏蔣干及太子智閉城拒守。

translations.literal: On the day guisi they reached Ye; Wei's Jiang Gan and Crown Prince Zhi shut the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi they reached Ye; Jiang Gan and Crown Prince Zhi barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 城外皆降於燕，劉寧及弟崇帥胡騎三千奔晉陽。

translations.literal: Outside the walls all submitted to Yan; Liu Ning and his younger brother Chong led three thousand Hu horsemen and fled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone outside the walls submitted. Liu Ning and his brother Chong fled to Jinyang with three thousand Hu cavalry.

sentences.zh: 秦以張遇為征東大將軍、豫州牧。

translations.literal: Qin appointed Zhang Yu Grand General Who Campaigns East and Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qin made Zhang Yu grand general who campaigns east and governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 五月，秦主健攻張琚於宜秋，斬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Qin ruler Jian attacked Zhang Ju at Yiqiu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Qin ruler Jian attacked Zhang Ju at Yiqiu and executed him.

sentences.zh: 鄴中大饑，人相食，故趙時宮人被食略盡。

translations.literal: In Ye there was great famine; men ate one another, and the palace women of former Zhao times were nearly all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Ye starved; people ate one another, and the palace women of Zhao were nearly all consumed.

sentences.zh: 蔣干遺侍中繆嵩、詹事劉猗奉表請降，且求救於謝尚。

translations.literal: Jiang Gan sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Miao Song and Household Mentor Liu Yi bearing a memorial to request surrender, and also to beg rescue from Xie Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gan sent Miao Song and Liu Yi with a surrender memorial and a plea for help to Xie Shang.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，燕王俊遣廣威將軍慕容軍、殿中將軍慕輿根、右司馬皇甫真等帥步騎二萬助慕容評攻鄴。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Murong Jun of Yan sent Broad Prestige General Murong Jun, Palace General Muyu Gen, Right Major Huangfu Zhen, and others leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to assist Murong Ping in attacking Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, Jun sent Murong Jun, Muyu Gen, Huangfu Zhen, and others with twenty thousand men to reinforce Ping at Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，燕人斬冉閔於龍城。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the Yan beheaded Ran Min at Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, the Yan beheaded Ran Min at Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 會大旱，蝗，燕王俊謂閔為祟，遣使祀之，謚曰悼武天王。

translations.literal: Just then there was great drought and locusts; Murong Jun of Yan thought Min was haunting him, sent envoys to sacrifice to him, and gave him the posthumous title Lamented Martial Heavenly King.
translations.idiomatic: A drought and locust plague followed. Jun believed Min's ghost was to blame, sacrificed to him, and gave him the posthumous title Lamented Martial Heavenly King.

sentences.zh: 初，謝尚使戴施據枋頭，施聞蔣干求救，乃自倉垣徙屯棘津，止干使者求傳國璽。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xie Shang had sent Dai Shi to hold Fangtou; when Shi heard Jiang Gan begging for rescue, he moved from Cangyuan to encamp at Jijin, detained Gan's envoy, and demanded the imperial transmission seal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xie Shang had posted Dai Shi at Fangtou. Hearing Jiang Gan's plea for aid, Shi moved to Jijin and detained Gan's envoy to demand the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 劉猗使繆嵩還鄴白干，干疑尚不能救，沈吟未決。

translations.literal: Liu Yi sent Miao Song back to Ye to inform Gan; Gan doubted that Shang could save him and hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi sent Miao Song back to Ye. Gan doubted Shang would come and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 六月，施帥壯士百餘人入鄴，助守三臺，紿之曰：「今燕寇在外，道路不通，璽未敢送也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Shi led more than a hundred stalwarts into Ye to help guard the Three Terraces, and deceived Gan, saying, "Now the Yan invaders are outside and the roads are blocked—I dare not send the seal yet.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Shi entered Ye with a hundred picked men to help hold the Three Terraces. He told Gan, "Yan armies block the roads—I cannot send the seal yet.

sentences.zh: 卿且出以付我，我當馳白天子。

translations.literal: For now bring it out and entrust it to me; I shall ride swiftly to inform the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Give it to me for safekeeping and I will ride to inform the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子聞璽在吾所，信卿至誠，必多發兵糧以相救餉。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven hears the seal is with me, he will trust your utmost sincerity and surely send abundant troops and grain to rescue and supply you.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor knows the seal is safe with me, he will trust your loyalty and send troops and grain.

sentences.zh: 」干以為然，出璽付之。

translations.literal: Gan thought this right and brought out the seal and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan agreed and handed over the seal.

sentences.zh: 施宣言使督護何融迎糧，陰令懷璽送於枋頭。

translations.literal: Shi publicly announced that he was sending Supervisor He Rong to welcome grain, but secretly ordered a man carrying the seal to deliver it to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi announced he was sending He Rong to fetch supplies, but secretly sent the seal to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，蔣干帥銳卒五千及晉兵出戰，慕容評大破之，斬首四千級，干脫走入城。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Jiang Gan led five thousand picked troops and Jin soldiers out to battle; Murong Ping routed them utterly, took four thousand heads, and Gan escaped back into the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Jiang Gan marched out with five thousand elite troops and Jin soldiers. Ping crushed them, took four thousand heads, and Gan fled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 甲申，秦主健還長安。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Qin ruler Jian returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Qin ruler Jian returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 謝尚、姚襄共攻張遇於許昌。

translations.literal: Xie Shang and Yao Xiang jointly attacked Zhang Yu at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang and Yao Xiang attacked Zhang Yu at Xuchang together.

sentences.zh: 秦主健遣丞相東海王雄、衛大將軍平昌王菁略地關東，帥步騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Jian sent Chancellor the Prince of Donghai, Xiong, and Defender Grand General the Prince of Pingchang, Jing, to seize territory east of the passes, leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Jian sent Chancellor Prince of Donghai Xiong and Defender-in-chief Prince of Pingchang Jing east of the passes with twenty thousand men to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，戰於穎水之誠橋，尚等大敗，死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai they fought at Chengqiao on the Ying River; Shang and the others were utterly defeated, and fifteen thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai they fought at Chengqiao on the Ying River. Shang was routed; fifteen thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 尚奔還淮南，襄棄輜重，送尚於芍陂；

translations.literal: Shang fled back to Huainan; Xiang abandoned baggage trains and escorted Shang to Shaopi;
translations.idiomatic: Shang fled to Huainan. Xiang abandoned the baggage train and escorted him to Shaopi;

sentences.zh: 尚悉以後事付襄。

translations.literal: Shang entrusted all remaining affairs to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang entrusted all his remaining affairs to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 殷浩聞尚敗，退屯壽春。

translations.literal: When Yin Hao heard that Shang was defeated, he withdrew to encamp at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Shang's defeat, Yin Hao withdrew to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦丞相雄徙張遇及陳、穎、許、洛之民五萬餘戶於關中，以右衛將軍楊群為豫州刺史，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Qin Chancellor Xiong moved Zhang Yu and more than fifty thousand households of the people of Chen, Ying, Xu, and Luo to Guanzhong, and made Right Defender General Yang Qun Inspector of Yu Province, garrisoning Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Chancellor Xiong relocated Zhang Yu and more than fifty thousand households from Chen, Ying, Xu, and Luo to Guanzhong, and posted Yang Qun as Yu inspector at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 謝尚降，號建威將軍。

translations.literal: Xie Shang submitted and was titled General Who Establishes Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang submitted and was made general who establishes prestige.

sentences.zh: 趙故西中郎將王擢遣使請降；

translations.literal: Wang Zhuo, former Western Gentlemen-of-the-House of Zhao, sent envoys to request surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Former Zhao Western Gentlemen Wang Zhuo sent envoys to surrender;

sentences.zh: 拜擢秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhuo was appointed Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was made Qin inspector.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以武陵王晞為太宰。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, the Prince of Wuling, Xi, was made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Prince of Wuling Xi was made grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，燕王俊如中山。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Murong Jun of Yan went to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Yan ruler Jun went to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 王午聞魏敗，時鄧恆已死，午自稱安國王。

translations.literal: When Wang Wu heard that Wei was defeated—Deng Heng had already died by then—Wu styled himself King Who Pacifies the State.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu, hearing of Wei's defeat—Deng Heng was already dead—styled himself King Who Pacifies the State.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰，燕王俊遣慕容恪、封弈、陽騖攻之，午閉城自守，送冉操詣燕軍；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wuchen, Murong Jun of Yan sent Murong Ke, Feng Yi, and Yang Xu to attack him; Wu shut the city and held out, and sent Ran Cao to the Yan army;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day wuchen, Jun sent Murong Ke, Feng Yi, and Yang Xu against him. Wu barred the gates and sent Ran Cao to the Yan camp;

sentences.zh: 燕人掠其禾稼而還。

translations.literal: the Yan men plundered his grain crops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: the Yan stripped his fields and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏長水校尉馬願等開鄴城納燕兵，戴施、蔣干懸縋而下，奔於倉垣。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Wei Changshui Colonel Ma Yuan and others opened Ye city to admit Yan troops; Dai Shi and Jiang Gan lowered themselves on ropes and fled to Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Former Wei Changshui Colonel Ma Yuan and others opened Ye to Yan forces. Dai Shi and Jiang Gan let themselves down on ropes and escaped to Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 慕容評送魏後董氏、太子智、太尉申鐘、司空條攸等及乘輿服御於薊。

translations.literal: Murong Ping sent Former Wei Empress Lady Dong, Crown Prince Zhi, Grand Commandant Shen Zhong, Minister of Works Tiao You, and others, together with the imperial carriage and regalia, to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping sent the Former Wei empress Lady Dong, Crown Prince Zhi, Grand Commandant Shen Zhong, Minister of Works Tiao You, and others, along with the imperial carriage and court regalia, to Ji.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王簡、左僕射張乾、右僕射郎肅皆自殺。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Wang Jian, Left Vice Director Zhang Qian, and Right Vice Director Lang Su all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Director of the Secretariat, Zhang Qian, Left Vice Director, and Lang Su, Right Vice Director, all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊詐云董氏得傳國璽獻之，賜號奉璽君，賜冉智爵海賓侯。

translations.literal: Yan's Murong Jun falsely claimed that Lady Dong had obtained and presented the Imperial Seal; he granted her the title Lady Who Offers the Seal and enfeoffed Ran Zhi as Marquis of Haibin.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun of Yan falsely announced that Lady Dong had found the Imperial Seal and presented it to him. He gave her the title Lady Who Offers the Seal and made Ran Zhi Marquis of Haibin.

sentences.zh: 以申鐘為大將軍右長史。

translations.literal: Shen Zhong was appointed Right Chief Clerk to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong was made Right Chief Clerk under the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 命慕容評鎮鄴。

translations.literal: Murong Ping was ordered to garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping was placed in command at Ye.

sentences.zh: 桓溫使司馬勳助周撫討蕭敬文於涪城，斬之。

translations.literal: Huan Wen sent Sima Xun to assist Zhou Fu in attacking Xiao Jingwen at Fucheng; Jingwen was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen dispatched Sima Xun to help Zhou Fu attack Xiao Jingwen at Fucheng. Jingwen was executed.

sentences.zh: 謝尚自枋頭迎傳國璽至建康，百僚畢賀。

translations.literal: Xie Shang personally went from Fangtou to welcome the Imperial Seal to Jiankang; all officials congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang went in person from Fangtou to escort the Imperial Seal to Jiankang, and the entire bureaucracy offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 秦以雷弱兒為大司馬，毛貴為太尉，張遇為司空。

translations.literal: Qin appointed Lei Ruo'er Grand Marshal, Mao Gui Grand Commandant, and Zhang Yu Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin named Lei Ruo'er Grand Marshal, Mao Gui Grand Commandant, and Zhang Yu Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 殷浩之北伐也，中軍將軍王羲之以書止之，不聽。

translations.literal: When Yin Hao undertook his northern expedition, Central Army General Wang Xizhi wrote to dissuade him, but Hao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: During Yin Hao's northern campaign, Central Army General Wang Xizhi wrote urging him to stop, but Hao refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 既而無功，復謀再舉。

translations.literal: When it came to nothing, they again plotted to launch another campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After the failure, they planned to mount another offensive.

sentences.zh: 羲之遺浩書曰：「今以區區江左，天下寒心，固已久矣。

translations.literal: Xizhi sent Hao a letter saying: "Today this petty region south of the Yangtze has long been the object of the world's anxious concern.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi wrote to Yin Hao: "This small realm south of the Yangtze has for a long time been a source of anxiety throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 力爭武功，非所當作。

translations.literal: Striving for military glory is not what should be done.
translations.idiomatic: To strain after martial achievement is not what you ought to do now.

sentences.zh: 自頃處內外之任者，未有深謀遠慮，而疲竭根本，各從所志，竟無一功可論，遂令天下將有土崩之勢。

translations.literal: Of late those holding inner and outer responsibilities have shown no deep planning or far-sighted counsel, but have worn out the foundation, each pursuing his own inclinations, and in the end not one achievement can be named—so that the realm is now on the brink of collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the men charged with affairs at court and in the field have lacked foresight, yet they have exhausted the state's roots, each following his own whim, until not a single success can be cited—and the empire now stands on the verge of disintegration.

sentences.zh: 任其事者，豈得辭四海之責哉！

translations.literal: Can those charged with this affair shirk responsibility to the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: Surely those who bear this burden cannot evade blame before all under heaven!

sentences.zh: 今軍破於外，資竭於內，保淮之志，非所復及，莫若還保長江，督將各處復舊鎮。

translations.literal: Now the army is defeated abroad and resources exhausted within; the will to hold the Huai is no longer attainable. Better to withdraw and secure the Yangtze, and have each commander return to his old post.
translations.idiomatic: The army has been broken in the field and supplies are spent at home. The ambition to defend the Huai can no longer be sustained. You should fall back and hold the Yangtze, and order each general to resume his former garrison.

sentences.zh: 自長江以外，羈縻而已。

translations.literal: Beyond the Yangtze, mere loose control would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river, loose suzerainty would be enough.

sentences.zh: 引咎責躬，更為善治，省其賦役，與民更始，庶可以救倒懸之急也！

translations.literal: Accept blame, reflect on yourself, govern well anew, lighten taxes and corvée, and begin anew with the people—then perhaps the crisis of hanging upside down can be saved!
translations.idiomatic: Take blame upon yourself, reform your rule, reduce levies and labor, and make a fresh start with the people—only then may this peril, acute as a man hanging by his heels, be relieved!

sentences.zh: 使君起於布衣，任天下之重，當董統之任，而敗喪至此，恐闔朝群賢未有與人分其謗者。

translations.literal: You, sir, rose from commoner status to bear the weight of the realm and shoulder the director's role, yet defeat has reached this point—I fear no one among the court's worthies will share your blame.
translations.idiomatic: You began as a commoner and were entrusted with the fate of the realm, charged to lead the state—yet ruin has come to this pass. I doubt any worthy at court will divide your disgrace with you.

sentences.zh: 若猶以前事為未工，故復求之分外，宇宙雖廣，自容何所！

translations.literal: If you still think the previous affair was not enough effort and therefore seek more beyond your measure—even though the cosmos is vast, where will you find room for yourself!
translations.idiomatic: If you still believe the last campaign was not pushed hard enough and therefore reach for tasks beyond your strength—even in so wide a world, where will you find a place to hide!

sentences.zh: 此愚智所不解也。

translations.literal: This is what neither the foolish nor the wise can understand.
translations.idiomatic: That is something neither fool nor sage can fathom.

sentences.zh: 又與會稽王昱箋曰：「為人臣者誰不願尊其主比隆前世！

translations.literal: He also wrote to Prince of Kuaiji Wang Yu: "What subject does not wish to exalt his lord to rival past ages!
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a letter to Prince Kuaiji Wang Yu: "What minister does not wish to raise his sovereign to the glory of former dynasties!

sentences.zh: 況遇難得之運哉！

translations.literal: How much more when one meets a seldom-given opportunity!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when fortune offers a chance so rare!

sentences.zh: 顧力有所不及，豈不可不權輕重而處之也！

translations.literal: Seeing that strength falls short, should one not weigh light and heavy and act accordingly!
translations.idiomatic: When one sees that power is insufficient, should one not measure what is light against what is heavy and act accordingly!

sentences.zh: 今雖有可喜之會，內求諸己，而所憂乃重於所喜。

translations.literal: Though there is now an occasion for joy, looking within oneself, one's worries outweigh one's joys.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are grounds for rejoicing, if you look within, your anxieties outweigh your satisfactions.

sentences.zh: 功未可期，遺黎殲盡，勞役無時，徵求日重，以區區吳、越經緯天下十分之九，不亡何待！

translations.literal: Success is not yet expected; the surviving people are destroyed; corvée never ceases; exactions grow daily—with meager Wu and Yue carrying nine-tenths of the realm's burdens, how can we not perish!
translations.idiomatic: Victory is still remote, the remnant population is being consumed, labor service never ends, and levies grow heavier by the day—yet tiny Wu and Yue must bear nine-tenths of the empire's weight. How can we escape ruin!

sentences.zh: 而不度德量力，不弊不己，此封內所痛心歎悼而莫敢吐誠者也。

translations.literal: Yet without measuring virtue against strength, not stopping until ruined—this is what those within the realm bitterly lament yet dare not speak openly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you refuse to weigh your virtue against your strength and will not stop until all is broken—this is what the people within your domain mourn in silence, too afraid to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 『往者不可諫，來者猶可追。

translations.literal: 'What is past cannot be admonished; what is to come may yet be pursued.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The past cannot be changed, but the future may still be amended.'

sentences.zh: 』願殿下更垂三思，先為不可勝之基，鬚根立勢舉，謀之未晚。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will reflect further; first lay a foundation that cannot be defeated, let roots grow and authority stand firm, and plan—not too late.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Highness to think again and again: first establish a base that cannot be overcome, let roots take hold and power stand firm, and only then move—there is still time.

sentences.zh: 若不行，恐糜鹿之遊，將不止林藪而已！

translations.literal: If this is not done, I fear the wanderings of elk will not be confined to forests and marshes alone!
translations.idiomatic: If you do not, I fear the roaming of elk will not stop at woods and thickets alone!

sentences.zh: 願殿下暫廢虛遠之懷，以救倒懸之急，可謂以亡為存，轉禍為福也。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will for a time set aside lofty distant ambitions and rescue the crisis of hanging upside down—this may be said to turn death into life and misfortune into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Highness to lay aside for now your far-reaching schemes and relieve this peril, acute as a man hanging by his heels—to do so would be to turn death into life and disaster into good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: They did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was not followed.

sentences.zh: 九月，浩屯泗口，遣河南太守戴施據石門，滎陽太守劉遯據倉垣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Hao camped at Sikou, sent Henan Administrator Dai Shi to hold Shimen, and Xingyang Administrator Liu Zun to hold Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yin Hao encamped at Sikou. He sent Henan Administrator Dai Shi to occupy Shimen and Xingyang Administrator Liu Zun to hold Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 浩以軍興，罷遣太學生徒，學校由此遂廢。

translations.literal: Because of the military campaign, Hao dismissed the students of the Imperial Academy, and schools were thereby abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: To supply the army, Yin Hao dismissed the students of the Imperial University, and formal schooling lapsed from that time.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，謝尚遣冠軍將軍王俠攻許昌，克之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Xie Shang sent Champion General Wang Xia to attack Xuchang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Xie Shang dispatched Champion General Wang Xia against Xuchang. The city fell.

sentences.zh: 秦豫州刺史楊群退屯弘農。

translations.literal: Qin's Inspector of Yuzhou Yang Qun withdrew to garrison Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qun, Inspector of Yuzhou for Former Qin, fell back to defend Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 徵尚為給事中，戍石頭。

translations.literal: Xie Shang was summoned as Attendant Within; he garrisoned Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang was recalled to serve as Attendant Within the Palace and took up garrison duty at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，燕王俊還薊。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Murong Jun of Yan returned to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Murong Jun of Yan returned to Ji.

sentences.zh: 故趙將擁兵據州郡者，各遣使降燕；

translations.literal: Former Zhao generals who held troops and occupied prefectures and commanderies each sent envoys to submit to Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Former Zhao commanders who still held armies and controlled prefectures and commanderies each sent envoys to surrender to Yan;

sentences.zh: 燕王俊以王擢為益州刺史，夔逸為秦州刺史，張平為并州刺史，李歷為兗州刺史，高昌為安西將軍，劉寧為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Murong Jun appointed Wang Zhuo Inspector of Yizhou, Kui Yi Inspector of Qinzhou, Zhang Ping Inspector of Bingzhou, Li Li Inspector of Yanzhou, Gao Chang General Who Guards the West, and Liu Ning General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun named Wang Zhuo Inspector of Yizhou, Kui Yi Inspector of Qinzhou, Zhang Ping Inspector of Bingzhou, Li Li Inspector of Yanzhou, Gao Chang General Who Guards the West, and Liu Ning General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 慕容恪屯安平，積糧，治攻具，將討王午。

translations.literal: Murong Ke garrisoned Anping, accumulated grain, prepared siege equipment, and intended to attack Wang Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke encamped at Anping, stockpiled grain, readied siege engines, and prepared to attack Wang Wu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，中山蘇林起兵於無極，自稱天子；

translations.literal: On bingxu, Su Lin of Zhongshan rose in Wuji and proclaimed himself emperor;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Su Lin of Zhongshan rebelled at Wuji and declared himself emperor;

sentences.zh: 恪自魯口還討林。

translations.literal: Ke returned from Lukou to attack Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Ke marched back from Lukou to suppress Lin.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊子，燕王俊遣廣威將軍慕輿根助恪攻林，斬之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, Murong Jun sent General of Broad Authority Murong Gen to assist Ke in attacking Lin; Lin was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuzi, Murong Jun dispatched General of Broad Authority Murong Gen to help Ke attack Lin. Lin was executed.

sentences.zh: 王午為其將秦興所殺。

translations.literal: Wang Wu was killed by his general Qin Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wu was slain by his own officer Qin Xing.

sentences.zh: 呂護殺興，復自稱安國王。

translations.literal: Lü Hu killed Xing and again styled himself King of An'guo.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hu murdered Xing and once more proclaimed himself King of An'guo.

sentences.zh: 燕群僚共上尊號於燕王俊，俊許之。

translations.literal: Yan's officials collectively offered Murong Jun a supreme title; Jun consented.
translations.idiomatic: The officials of Yan jointly urged Murong Jun to accept an imperial title, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，始置百官，以國相封弈為太尉，左長史陽騖為尚書令，右司馬皇甫真為尚書左僕射，典書令張悕為右僕射；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, he first established the hundred officials—Grand Chancellor Feng Yi as Grand Commandant, Left Chief Clerk Yang Yu as Secretariat Director, Right Marshal Huangfu Zhen as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Director of Documents Zhang Xi as Right Vice Director;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, he first installed the full bureaucracy: Grand Chancellor Feng Yi became Grand Commandant, Left Chief Clerk Yang Yu Secretariat Director, Right Marshal Huangfu Zhen Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Director of Documents Zhang Xi Right Vice Director;

sentences.zh: 其餘文武，拜授有差。

translations.literal: The rest of civil and military officials received appointments in due gradation.
translations.idiomatic: All other civil and military officers were promoted and assigned according to rank.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，俊即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Jun ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Murong Jun took the imperial throne and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 自謂獲傳國璽，改元元璽。

translations.literal: Claiming he had obtained the Imperial Seal, he changed the era name to Yuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Because he believed he possessed the Imperial Seal, he adopted the era name Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 追尊武宣王為高祖武宣皇帝，文明王為太祖文明皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored the Martial Accomplishment King as High Ancestor Martial Accomplishment Emperor and the Civilized King as Grand Ancestor Civilized Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated the Martial Accomplishment King posthumously to High Ancestor Martial Accomplishment Emperor and the Civilized King to Grand Ancestor Civilized Emperor.

sentences.zh: 時晉使適至燕，俊謂曰：「汝還，白汝天子：我承人乏，為中國所推，已為帝矣！

translations.literal: At that time a Jin envoy happened to arrive in Yan; Jun said to him: "Go back and tell your Son of Heaven: burdened by the people's need, pushed by China, I have already become emperor!
translations.idiomatic: A Jin envoy happened to arrive in Yan just then. Murong Jun told him: "Return and inform your Son of Heaven: pressed by the people's want and acclaimed within China, I have already become emperor!

sentences.zh: 」改司州為中州，建留臺於龍都，以玄菟太守乙逸為尚書，專委留務。

translations.literal: He changed Sizhou to Zhongzhou, established a capital office at Longdu, and appointed Commandant of Xuantu Yi Yi as Secretariat official to entrust him with affairs at the capital office.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Sizhou Zhongzhou, set up a secondary capital at Longdu, and appointed Yi Yi, Commandant of Xuantu, as Secretariat officer with full charge of affairs there.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄攻王擢於隴西，擢奔涼州，雄還屯隴東。

translations.literal: Qin Chancellor Xiong attacked Wang Zhuo in Longxi; Zhuo fled to Liangzhou, and Xiong returned to camp in Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin's Chancellor Fu Xiong attacked Wang Zhuo in Longxi. Zhuo fled to Liangzhou, and Xiong withdrew to encamp in Longdong.

sentences.zh: 張重華以擢為征虜將軍、秦州刺史，特寵待之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua appointed Zhuo as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Qinzhou, treating him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua made Zhuo General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Qinzhou and treated him with special honor.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯朔，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, first day yimao—general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the first day yimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 二月，庚子，燕王俊立其妃可足渾氏為皇后，世子曄為皇太子，皆自龍城遷於薊宮。

translations.literal: Second month, gengzi—Murong Jun installed his consort Lady Kebulun as empress and heir apparent Ye as crown prince; both moved from Longcheng to the Ji palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on gengzi, Murong Jun installed his consort Lady Kebulun as empress and his heir Ye as crown prince. Both were moved from Longcheng into the palace at Ji.

sentences.zh: 張重華遣將軍張弘、宋修會王擢帥騎萬五千伐秦。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua sent generals Zhang Hong and Song Xiu to join Wang Zhuo in leading fifteen thousand cavalry to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua dispatched Generals Zhang Hong and Song Xiu to join Wang Zhuo in leading fifteen thousand horsemen against Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄、衛將軍菁拒之，大敗涼兵於龍黎，斬首萬二千級，虜張弘、宋修，王擢棄秦州，奔姑臧。

translations.literal: Qin Chancellor Xiong and Guard General Jing resisted them; they utterly defeated Liang forces at Longli, beheading twelve thousand, capturing Zhang Hong and Song Xiu; Wang Zhuo abandoned Qinzhou and fled to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Fu Xiong and Guard General Fu Jing met them and routed the Liang army at Longli, taking twelve thousand heads and capturing Zhang Hong and Song Xiu. Wang Zhuo abandoned Qinzhou and fled to Guzang.

sentences.zh: 秦主健以領軍將軍苻願為秦州刺史，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Jian appointed Guards General Fu Yuan as Inspector of Qinzhou to garrison Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian appointed Guards General Fu Yuan Inspector of Qinzhou and stationed him at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 三月，交州刺史阮敷討林邑，破五十餘壘。

translations.literal: Third month—Inspector of Jiaozhou Ruan Fu attacked Linyi and broke more than fifty fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Inspector of Jiaozhou Ruan Fu attacked Linyi and stormed more than fifty strongholds.

sentences.zh: 趙故衛尉常山李犢聚眾數千人叛燕。

translations.literal: Former Zhao Commandant of the Guards Li Du of Changshan gathered several thousand men and rebelled against Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du of Changshan, former Commandant of the Guards under Zhao, mustered several thousand men and rebelled against Yan.

sentences.zh: 西域胡劉康詐稱劉曜子，聚眾於平陽，自稱晉王；

translations.literal: A Western Regions barbarian Liu Kang falsely claimed to be the son of Liu Yao, gathered a host at Pingyang, and styled himself King of Jin;
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian from the Western Regions, Liu Kang, falsely claimed to be Liu Yao's son, raised troops at Pingyang, and proclaimed himself King of Jin;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦左衛將軍苻飛討擒之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month—Qin Left Guards General Fu Fei captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Former Qin's Left Guards General Fu Fei seized him.

sentences.zh: 以安西將軍謝尚為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Xie Shang was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang, General Who Guards the West, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五月，張重華復使王擢帥眾二萬伐上邽，秦州郡縣多應之；

translations.literal: Fifth month—Zhang Chonghua again sent Wang Zhuo with twenty thousand troops to attack Shanggui; many Qin prefectures and commanderies responded;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhang Chonghua again sent Wang Zhuo with twenty thousand men against Shanggui. Many Qin prefectures and commanderies rose in his support;

sentences.zh: 苻願戰敗，奔長安。

translations.literal: Fu Yuan was defeated in battle and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yuan was beaten in battle and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 重華因上疏請伐秦。

translations.literal: Chonghua therefore memorialized requesting permission to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua thereupon submitted a memorial asking leave to campaign against Qin.

sentences.zh: 詔進重華涼州牧。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Chonghua to Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict promoted Chonghua to Governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 燕主俊遣衛將軍恪討李犢，犢降，遂東擊呂護於魯口。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Jun sent Guard General Ke to attack Li Du; Du submitted, then Ke marched east to attack Lü Hu at Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun sent Guard General Murong Ke against Li Du. Du surrendered, and Ke then marched east to attack Lü Hu at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 六月，秦苻飛攻氐王楊初於仇池，為初所敗。

translations.literal: Sixth month—Qin Fu Fei attacked Di king Yang Chu at Qiuchi and was defeated by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Fu Fei of Former Qin attacked the Di chieftain Yang Chu at Qiuchi and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 丞相雄、平昌王菁帥步騎四萬屯於隴東。

translations.literal: Chancellor Xiong and Prince of Pingchang Jing led forty thousand infantry and cavalry to camp in Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Fu Xiong and Prince of Pingchang Fu Jing led forty thousand foot and horse to encamp in Longdong.

sentences.zh: 秦主健納張遇繼母韓氏為昭儀，數於眾中謂遇曰：「卿，吾假子也。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Jian took Zhang Yu's stepmother Lady Han as Brilliant Companion; several times before the assembly he said to Yu: "You, sir, are my adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian took Zhang Yu's stepmother Lady Han as Brilliant Companion. More than once before the court he told Yu: "You are my adopted son.

sentences.zh: 」遇恥之，因雄等精兵在外，陰結關中豪傑，欲滅苻氏，以其地來降。

translations.literal: Yu was shamed by this; because Xiong and others had elite troops outside, he secretly joined with Guanzhong notables, intending to destroy the Fu clan and submit their territory in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was humiliated. With Xiong and the other commanders holding crack troops in the field, he secretly allied with the leading families of Guanzhong, plotting to overthrow the Fu house and offer the land in submission.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，遇與黃門劉晁謀夜襲健，晃約開門以待之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month—Yu plotted with Palace Attendant Liu Chao to attack Jian by night; Chao agreed to open the gate and wait.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Yu conspired with Palace Attendant Liu Chao for a night assault on Fu Jian. Chao promised to open the gate and admit them.

sentences.zh: 會健使晃出外，晃固辭，不得已而行。

translations.literal: It happened that Jian sent Chao out on a mission; Chao firmly declined but in the end had to go.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Fu Jian sent Chao away on business. Chao pleaded to stay but was compelled to leave.

sentences.zh: 遇不知，引兵至門，門不開。

translations.literal: Yu did not know this; he led troops to the gate, but the gate did not open.
translations.idiomatic: Yu knew nothing of this. He brought his force to the gate, but the gate remained shut.

sentences.zh: 事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed, and both men were put to death.

sentences.zh: 於是孔持起池陽，劉珍、夏侯顯起鄠，喬秉起雍，胡陽赤起司竹，呼延毒起灞城，眾數萬人，各遣使來請兵。

translations.literal: Then Kong Chi rose in Chiyang, Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian in Hu, Qiao Bing in Yong, Hu Yangchi in Sizhu, and Huyan Du in Bacheng—hosts of tens of thousands each sent envoys to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Kong Chi rebelled at Chiyang; Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian at Hu; Qiao Bing at Yong; Hu Yangchi at Sizhu; and Huyan Du at Bacheng. Each raised tens of thousands of men and sent envoys asking for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 秦以左僕射魚遵為司空。

translations.literal: Qin appointed Left Vice Director Yu Zun Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin appointed Left Vice Director Yu Zun Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦丞相雄帥眾二萬還長安，遣平昌王菁略定上洛，置荊州於豐陽川，以步兵校尉金城郭敬為刺史。

translations.literal: Ninth month—Chancellor Xiong led twenty thousand troops back to Chang'an, sent Prince of Pingchang Jing to pacify Shangluo, established Jingzhou in Fengyangchuan, and appointed Infantry Commandant Jin Cheng Jingui as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chancellor Xiong returned to Chang'an with twenty thousand men, sent Prince of Pingchang Jing to secure Shangluo, established Jingzhou along the Fengyang River, and named Infantry Commandant Jin Cheng Jingui its inspector.

sentences.zh: 雄與清河王法、苻飛分討孔持等。

translations.literal: Xiong with Prince of Qinghe Fa and Fu Fei divided forces to attack Kong Chi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, together with Prince of Qinghe Fu Fa and Fu Fei, split their armies to suppress Kong Chi and the rest.

sentences.zh: 姚襄屯歷陽，以燕、秦方強，未有北伐之志，乃夾淮廣興屯田，訓厲將士。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang garrisoned Liyang; seeing Yan and Qin newly strong, he had no wish for a northern expedition, so along both banks of the Huai he widely established garrison farms and drilled his officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang was stationed at Liyang. With Yan and Qin growing powerful, he had no mind for a northern campaign. Instead he opened large garrison farms along both sides of the Huai and trained his troops.

sentences.zh: 殷浩在壽春，惡其強盛，囚襄諸弟，屢遣刺客刺之，刺客皆以情告襄。

translations.literal: Yin Hao was at Shouchun and hated Xiang's strength; he imprisoned Xiang's younger brothers and repeatedly sent assassins to stab him—the assassins each informed Xiang of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, at Shouchun, resented Yao Xiang's power. He imprisoned Xiang's younger brothers and sent assassins again and again; each assassin confessed the plot to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍魏統卒，弟憬代領部曲。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Wei Tong died; his younger brother Jing succeeded to his command.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North Wei Tong died, and his younger brother Wei Jing took over his forces.

sentences.zh: 浩潛遣憬帥眾五千襲之，襄斬憬，並其眾。

translations.literal: Hao secretly sent Jing with five thousand men to surprise Xiang; Xiang beheaded Jing and absorbed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao secretly dispatched Wei Jing with five thousand men to strike Xiang by surprise. Xiang killed Jing and incorporated his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 浩愈惡之，使龍驤將軍劉啟守譙，遷襄於梁國蠡臺，表授梁國內史。

translations.literal: Hao hated him all the more, sent Flying Dragon General Liu Qi to guard Qiao, and moved Xiang to Li Terrace in Liang commandery, memorializing to appoint him Administrator of Liang within the state.
translations.idiomatic: Hao hated him still more. He posted Flying Dragon General Liu Qi at Qiao, transferred Xiang to Li Terrace in Liang, and memorialized to make him Administrator of Liang.

sentences.zh: 魏憬子弟數往來壽春，襄益疑懼，遣參軍權翼使於浩。

translations.literal: Wei Jing's sons and nephews often came and went to Shouchun; Xiang grew more suspicious and fearful, and sent aide Quan Yi as envoy to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jing's sons and nephews traveled frequently to Shouchun. Xiang grew increasingly uneasy and sent his aide Quan Yi to Yin Hao.

sentences.zh: 浩曰：「身與姚平北共為王臣，休戚同之。

translations.literal: Hao said: "I and Pacifier of the North Yao are alike subjects of the king; we share weal and woe.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Pacifier of the North Yao and I are both servants of the throne. Our fortunes are bound together.

sentences.zh: 平北每舉動自專，甚失輔車之理，豈所望也！

translations.literal: Pacifier of the North acts on his own initiative in every move—this greatly violates the principle of mutual support; how can this be what one hopes for!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he acts on his own in every matter, which utterly breaks the bond that should join us. How can that be what anyone wishes!

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「平北英姿絕世，擁兵數萬而遠歸晉室者，以朝廷有道，宰輔明哲故也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Pacifier of the North's heroic bearing is unmatched in the age; that he leads tens of thousands of troops and returns from afar to the Jin court is because the dynasty has the Way and the chief ministers are wise and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi replied: "Pacifier of the North's brilliance is unequaled in our time. That he commands tens of thousands of men and has come from afar to serve Jin is because the court holds to the Way and its leaders are wise.

sentences.zh: 今將軍輕信讒慝之言，與平北有隙，愚謂猜嫌之端，在此不在彼也。

translations.literal: Now the general lightly believes slanderous words and has a rift with Pacifier of the North—I think the root of suspicion lies here, not there.
translations.idiomatic: Now you lend credence to malicious talk and turn against him. I believe the source of distrust is on this side, not on his.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「平北姿性豪邁，生殺自由，又縱小人掠奪吾馬。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Pacifier of the North's nature is bold and unrestrained; he kills at will, and moreover indulges petty men in seizing my horses.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "His temperament is proud and violent. He puts people to death as he pleases, and he even lets his followers steal my horses.

sentences.zh: 王臣之體，固若是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how a subject of the king should behave?
translations.idiomatic: Is that the conduct of a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「平北歸命聖朝，豈肯妄殺無辜！

translations.literal: Yi said: "Pacifier of the North has submitted to the holy court—how could he carelessly kill the innocent!
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi said: "Having submitted to the sacred court, how could he slaughter the innocent at random!

sentences.zh: 奸宄之人，亦王法所不容也，殺之何害！

translations.literal: Wicked men are also what royal law does not tolerate; what harm in killing them!
translations.idiomatic: Villains are precisely what the law condemns. What wrong is there in executing them!

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「然則掠馬何也？

translations.literal: Hao said: "Then what of seizing the horses?
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Then what of the stolen horses?"

sentences.zh: 」翼曰：「將軍謂平北雄武難制，終將討之，故取馬欲以自衛耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The general considers Pacifier of the North too formidable to control and will eventually attack him; therefore he took the horses intending to protect himself."
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi said: "You regard Pacifier of the North as too strong to govern and expect one day to move against him. He seized the horses only to defend himself."

sentences.zh: 」浩笑曰：「何至是也！

translations.literal: Hao laughed and said: "Why would it come to that!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao laughed and said, "Surely it need not go that far!"

sentences.zh: 初，浩陰遣人誘秦梁安、雷弱兒，使殺秦主健，許以關右之任，弱兒偽許之，且請兵應接。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Hao secretly sent men to entice Qin generals Liang An and Lei Ruor, to have them kill Qin lord Jian, promising them charge of Guanyou; Ruor falsely agreed and also requested troops for liaison.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hao had secretly sent agents to win over the Former Qin generals Liang An and Lei Ruor, urging them to assassinate Emperor Jian in exchange for authority over the Guanzhong region. Ruor pretended to consent and asked for reinforcements to coordinate the strike.

sentences.zh: 浩聞張遇作亂，健兄子輔國將軍黃眉自洛陽西奔，以為安等事已成。

translations.literal: When Hao heard Zhang Yu had risen in rebellion and Jian's elder brother's son, Assistant-state General Huang Mei, had fled west from Luoyang, he thought An and the others' affair had succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Hao that Zhang Yu had rebelled and that Huang Mei, Jian's nephew and Assistant-state General, had fled west from Luoyang, Hao assumed Liang An's plot had already succeeded.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，浩自壽春帥眾七萬北伐，欲進據洛陽，修復園陵。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Hao led seventy thousand men north from Shouchun, intending to seize Luoyang and restore the imperial mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Hao marched north from Shouchun at the head of seventy thousand troops, aiming to take Luoyang and restore the Jin imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王彪之上會稽王昱箋，以為：「弱兒等容有詐偽，浩未應輕進。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Biaozhi submitted a memorial to Prince of Kuaiji Sima Yu, stating: "Ruor and the rest may well be practicing deception; Hao ought not advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi, Minister of Personnel, wrote to Prince Yu of Kuaiji warning that Ruor's pledge might be a ruse and that Hao should not rush his advance.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: [The advice] was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 浩以姚襄為前驅。

translations.literal: Hao made Yao Xiang his vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Hao appointed Yao Xiang to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 襄引兵北行，度浩將至，詐令部眾夜遁，陰伏甲以邀之。

translations.literal: Xiang led his troops north; estimating Hao was about to arrive, he falsely ordered his forces to flee by night and secretly set ambush troops to waylay him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang marched north, and when he judged Hao was near, he staged a night retreat while hiding armed men to spring an ambush.

sentences.zh: 浩聞而追襄至山桑。

translations.literal: On hearing this, Hao pursued Xiang as far as Shansang.
translations.idiomatic: Hao gave chase upon hearing the report and pursued Xiang to Shansang.

sentences.zh: 襄縱兵擊之，浩大敗，棄輜重，走保譙城。

translations.literal: Xiang loosed his troops to strike him; Hao suffered a great defeat, abandoned baggage train, and fled to hold Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang counterattacked in force. Hao was routed, abandoned his supply train, and fled to the refuge of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 襄俘斬萬餘，悉收其資仗，使兄益守山桑，襄復加淮南。

translations.literal: Xiang captured and beheaded more than ten thousand, took all their materiel and arms, left his elder brother Yi to guard Shansang, and Xiang again advanced into Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang killed or captured more than ten thousand men, seized their weapons and stores, left his brother Yi to hold Shansang, and pushed once more into Huainan.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱謂王彪之曰：「君言無不中，張、陳無以過也！

translations.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Yu said to Wang Biaozhi: "Sir, your words never miss; Zhang Liang and Chen Ping could not surpass you!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu told Biaozhi, "Your predictions never fail. You stand with Zhang Liang and Chen Ping themselves."

sentences.zh: 」西平敬烈公張重華有疾，子曜靈才十歲，立為世子，赦其境內。

translations.literal: Western Pacifier and Respected Duke Zhang Chonghua fell ill; his son Yaoling was only ten and was installed as heir apparent; amnesty was proclaimed within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua, Duke Jinglie of Xiping, took ill. His son Yaoling, only ten years old, was named heir, and a general amnesty was declared throughout the domain.

sentences.zh: 重華庶兄長寧侯祚，有勇力、吏干，而傾巧善事內外，與重華嬖臣趙長、尉緝等結異姓兄弟。

translations.literal: Chonghua's elder half-brother, Marquis Changning Zhang Zuo, had courage and strength and skill in administration, but was crafty and skilled at currying favor inside and out; he allied with Chonghua's favorites Zhao Chang and Wei Ji and others in a sworn brotherhood not of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua's older half-brother Zhang Zuo, Marquis of Changning, was bold, capable, and politically shrewd. He cultivated court insiders and outsiders alike and formed a sworn brotherhood with favorites such as Zhao Chang and Wei Ji.

sentences.zh: 都尉常據請出之，重華曰：「吾方以祚為周公，使輔幼子，君是何言也！

translations.literal: Commandant Chang Ju asked that he be expelled; Chonghua said: "I am just now taking Zuo to be the Duke of Zhou to assist the young son — what words are these, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Chang Ju urged that Zuo be sent away. Chonghua replied, "I mean to make Zuo my Duke of Zhou to guide my young heir. What sort of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 謝艾以枹罕之功有寵於重華，左右疾之，譖艾，出為酒泉太守。

translations.literal: Xie Ai, for his merit at Baohan, enjoyed Chonghua's favor; those about the throne resented him, slandered Ai, and he was sent out as Administrator of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai had won favor at court for his victory at Baohan, but rivals at Chonghua's side denounced him until he was banished to the post of Administrator of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 艾上疏言：「權幸用事，公室將危，乞聽臣入侍。

translations.literal: Ai submitted a memorial saying: "Powerful favorites hold sway; the ruling house will soon be endangered — I beg leave to return to attendance."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial Xie Ai warned that favored officials were steering the state toward ruin and begged permission to return to court.

sentences.zh: 」且言：「長寧侯祚及趙長等將為亂，宜盡逐之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Marquis Changning Zhang Zuo and Zhao Chang and the rest are about to rebel and ought all to be driven off."
translations.idiomatic: He also named Zhang Zuo and Zhao Chang as men plotting rebellion and urged that they be removed entirely.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，己未，重華疾甚，手令徵艾為衛將軍，監中外諸軍事，輔政；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day jiwei: Chonghua was gravely ill and by handwritten order summoned Ai as Palace Guard General, overseer of all military affairs within and without, to assist in government;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day of the eleventh month Chonghua was dying. By his own hand he summoned Xie Ai back as Palace Guard General and superintendent of all armies to share power at court;

sentences.zh: 祚、長等匿而不宜。

translations.literal: Zuo, Chang, and the rest concealed it and did not publish it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo and Zhao Chang suppressed the edict and never made it public.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，重華卒，世子曜靈立，稱大司馬、涼州刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: On dingmao Chonghua died; heir Yaoling was enthroned and styled himself Grand Marshal, Inspector of Liang province, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua died on dingmao. The young heir Yaoling took the throne, assuming the titles Grand Marshal, Inspector of Liang, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 趙長等矯重華遺令，以長寧侯祚為都督中外諸軍事、撫軍大將軍，輔政。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang and others forged Chonghua's deathbed order, making Marquis Changning Zhang Zuo Commander-in-chief of all forces within and without, Suppressing-armies Grand General, to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang and his faction forged a final testament naming Zhang Zuo supreme commander and Suppressing-armies Grand General, putting the regency in his hands.

sentences.zh: 殷浩使部將劉啟、王彬之攻姚益於山桑。

translations.literal: Yin Hao sent subordinate generals Liu Qi and Wang Bin to attack Yao Yi at Shansang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao ordered Liu Qi and Wang Binzhi to assault Yao Yi, Xiang's brother, at Shansang.

sentences.zh: 姚襄自淮南擊之，啟、彬之皆敗死。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang marched from Huainan to strike them; Qi and Bin both were defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang countered from Huainan and killed both generals in defeat.

sentences.zh: 襄進據芍陂。

translations.literal: Xiang advanced and seized Quebei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then seized the Quebei reservoir district.

sentences.zh: 趙末，樂陵朱禿、平原杜能、清河丁嬈、陽平孫元各擁兵分據城邑，至是皆請降於燕；

translations.literal: At the end of Zhao, Zhu Tu of Leling, Du Neng of Pingyuan, Ding Rao of Qinghe, and Sun Yuan of Yangping each held troops and occupied towns separately; by now all asked to surrender to Yan;
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Later Zhao, Zhu Tu, Du Neng, Ding Rao, and Sun Yuan had each seized local strongholds with private armies. Now all of them offered submission to Yan;

sentences.zh: 燕主俊以禿為青州刺史，能為平原太守，嬈為立節將軍，元為兗州刺史，各留撫其營。

translations.literal: Yan ruler Jun made Tu Inspector of Qing, Neng Administrator of Pingyuan, Rao Upright-integrity General, and Yuan Inspector of Yan; each was left to pacify his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun appointed them regional commanders but let each man retain his troops to keep his district quiet.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄克池陽，斬孔特。

translations.literal: Former Qin Chancellor Xiong took Chiyang and beheaded Kong Te.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong, Former Qin's chancellor, captured Chiyang and executed Kong Te.

sentences.zh: 十二月，清河王法、苻飛克鄠，斬劉珍、夏侯顯。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Prince of Qinghe Fu Fa and Fu Fei took E and beheaded Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fu Fa, Prince of Qinghe, and Fu Fei took the city of E and killed Liu Zhen and Xiahou Xian.

sentences.zh: 姚襄濟淮，屯盱眙，招掠流民，眾至七萬，分置守宰，勸課農桑；

translations.literal: Yao Xiang crossed the Huai, encamped at Xuyi, gathered and won over displaced people until his host reached seventy thousand; he set local officials and urged farming and sericulture;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang crossed the Huai to camp at Xuyi, where he gathered refugees until his force reached seventy thousand. He appointed officials, promoted agriculture, and restored order;

sentences.zh: 遣使詣建康罪狀殷浩，並自陳謝。

translations.literal: he sent envoys to Jiankang to indict Yin Hao and also to offer his own apology.
translations.idiomatic: and sent envoys to the Jin capital both to denounce Yin Hao and to plead his own case.

sentences.zh: 詔以謝尚都督江西、淮南諸軍事、豫州刺史，鎮歷陽。

translations.literal: An edict made Xie Shang overall commander of military affairs west of the river and in Huainan and Inspector of Yu, stationed at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Xie Shang commander on the Jiang-Huai front with his base at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 涼右長史趙長等建議，以為：「時難未夷，宜立長君，曜靈沖幼，請立長寧侯祚。

translations.literal: Liang's chief clerk Zhao Chang and others proposed, saying: "Times of hardship are not yet settled — a mature ruler ought to be installed; Yaoling is young and slight; we ask that Marquis Changning Zhang Zuo be enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chang and the Liang clerks argued that perilous times called for an adult ruler and asked that the throne go to Zhang Zuo rather than the child Yaoling.

sentences.zh: 」張祚先得幸於重華之母馬氏，馬氏許之，乃廢張曜靈為涼寧侯，立祚為大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuo had first won favor with Chonghua's mother Lady Ma; Lady Ma consented; then Zhang Yaoling was deposed as Marquis Ning of Liang and Zuo was established as Chief-commandant, Grand General, Governor of Liang province, and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo had already won over Chonghua's mother, Lady Ma. With her consent he deposed Yaoling to Marquis Ning of Liang and enthroned himself as grand commander, generalissimo, governor, and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 祚既得志，恣為淫虐，殺重華妃裴氏及謝艾。

translations.literal: Once Zuo had his will, he gave free rein to debauchery and cruelty, killing Chonghua's consort Lady Pei and Xie Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in power, Zhang Zuo indulged in cruelty, murdering Chonghua's consort Lady Pei and Xie Ai.

sentences.zh: 燕衛將軍恪、撫軍將軍軍、左將軍彪等屢薦給事黃門侍郎霸有命世之才，宜總大任。

translations.literal: Yan's Guard General Ke, Suppressing-armies General Jun, and Left General Biao and others repeatedly recommended Attendant of the Yellow Gate Murong Ba as having talent to order an age and fit to bear great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke, Murong Jun the Suppressing-armies General, Murong Biao, and other Yan officers repeatedly praised Murong Ba as a once-in-a-generation statesman worthy of supreme command.

sentences.zh: 是歲，燕主俊以霸為使持節、安東將軍、北冀州剌史，鎮常山。

translations.literal: That year Yan ruler Jun made Ba Commissioner bearing the Staff, Pacifying-the-east General, and Inspector of Northern Ji, stationed at Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Jun named Murong Ba Pacifier of the East and Inspector of Northern Ji, with his headquarters at Changshan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，張祚自稱涼王，改建興四十二年為和平元年。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Zhang Zuo styled himself King of Liang and changed the forty-second year of Jianxing to the first year of Peace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhang Zuo declared himself King of Liang and proclaimed a new era, renaming the forty-second year of Jianxing as the first year of Heping (Peace).

sentences.zh: 立妻辛氏為王后，子太和為太子，封弟天錫為長寧侯，子庭堅為建康侯，曜靈弟玄靚為涼武侯。

translations.literal: He installed his wife Lady Xin as queen, his son Taihe as crown prince, enfeoffed his younger brother Tiansi as Marquis Changning, his son Tingjian as Marquis Jiankang, and Yaoling's younger brother Xuanjing as Marquis Wuhou of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He named his wife Queen Xin, his son Taihe crown prince, and ennobled his kin, including his brother Tiansi and his nephew Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 置百官，郊祀天地，用天子禮樂。

translations.literal: He established the full bureaucracy, sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, and used the ritual music of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He filled out an imperial bureaucracy, performed suburban sacrifices, and adopted the rites and music reserved for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 尚書馬岌切諫，坐免官。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Ma Ji remonstrated sharply and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Director Ma Ji protested forcefully and was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 郎中丁琪復諫曰：「我自武公以來，世守臣節，抱忠履謙五十餘年，故能以一州大眾，抗舉世之虜，師徒歲起，民不告疲。

translations.literal: Gentleman Ding Qi remonstrated again, saying: "From Duke Wu downward we have generation after generation kept subject's integrity, embracing loyalty and practicing modesty for more than fifty years; therefore with one province's great multitude we could resist the invaders of the whole age, armies raised year after year, yet the people never complained of weariness."
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Ding Qi warned again: "Since Duke Wu our house has kept faith with Jin for fifty years. That loyalty let one province defy the empires of the north year after year without breaking the people."

sentences.zh: 殿下勳德未高於先公，而亟謀革命，臣未見其可也。

translations.literal: "Your Highness's merit and virtue are not yet higher than the former lords', yet you hasten to plot a change of mandate — your servant does not see how this can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "Your own achievements do not surpass your forebears', yet you rush toward usurpation. I see no hope in it."

sentences.zh: 彼士民所以用命，四遠所以歸向者，以吾能奉晉室故也。

translations.literal: "The reason officers and people obey and the four quarters turn to us is that we can serve the Jin house."
translations.idiomatic: "Officers and people obey us, and distant lands incline our way, only because we hold loyal to Jin."

sentences.zh: 今而自尊，則中外離心，安能以一隅之地，拒天下之強敵乎！

translations.literal: "Now if you exalt yourself, inside and outside will lose heart — how can you with a single corner's territory resist the strong enemies of all under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: "Raise yourself now and you shatter that bond. How will one corner of the realm stand against every great power in the land?"

sentences.zh: 」祚大怒，斬之於闕下。

translations.literal: Zuo was greatly enraged and had him beheaded below the gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo flew into a rage and had him executed before the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 故魏降將周成反，自宛襲洛陽。

translations.literal: Former Wei surrender general Zhou Cheng rebelled and struck Luoyang from Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cheng, a former Wei defector, rebelled and attacked Luoyang from Wan.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，河南太守戴施奔鮪渚。

translations.literal: On xinyou the Administrator of Henan Dai Shi fled to Wozhu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Henan administrator Dai Shi fled to Wozhu.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄克司竹。

translations.literal: Qin Chancellor Xiong took Sizhu.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin's chancellor Fu Xiong captured Sizhu.

sentences.zh: 胡陽赤奔霸城，依呼延毒。

translations.literal: Hu Yang Chi fled to Bacheng and relied on Huyan Du.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yang Chi fled to Bacheng and threw in his lot with Huyan Du.

sentences.zh: 中軍將軍、揚州刺史殷浩連年北伐，師徒屢敗，糧械都盡。

translations.literal: Central Army General and Inspector of Yang Yin Hao had for years campaigned north; army and master suffered repeated defeats and grain and arms were utterly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, Central Army General and Yangzhou inspector, had led repeated northern campaigns that ended in defeat after defeat until his armies were stripped of food and arms.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍桓溫因朝野之怨，上疏數浩之罪，請廢之。

translations.literal: Pacifying-the-west General Huan Wen, taking advantage of court and countryside resentment, submitted a memorial listing Hao's crimes and asking that he be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen seized on public anger to memorialize the throne with a tally of Hao's failures and demand his removal.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已，免浩為庶人，徙東陽之信安。

translations.literal: The court with no alternative stripped Hao of office and made him a commoner, banishing him to Xin'an in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court reluctantly cashiered him to commoner status and exiled him to Xin'an in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 自此內外大權一歸於溫矣。

translations.literal: From this the great power within and without all returned to Wen alone.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment power at court and in the provinces flowed to Huan Wen alone.

sentences.zh: 浩少與溫齊名，而心競不相下，溫常輕之。

translations.literal: Hao in youth had been equal in fame with Wen, but their hearts competed and neither would yield; Wen often slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: In their youth Yin Hao had matched Huan Wen in reputation, yet the two men rivaled each other relentlessly, and Wen held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 浩既廢黜，雖愁怨，不形辭色，常書空作「咄咄怪事」字。

translations.literal: Once Hao was deposed, though aggrieved and resentful he did not show it in word or countenance, and often wrote in the air the characters "duoduo guaishi" — "Alas, strange affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: After his fall Hao hid his bitterness behind an even face and would trace in the air the words "Alas — how strange!"

sentences.zh: 久之，溫謂掾郗超曰：「浩有德有言，向為令僕，足以儀刑百揆，朝廷用違其才耳。

translations.literal: After a long while Wen said to aide Xi Chao: "Hao has virtue and discourse; formerly as Director and Vice-director he could have been model to the hundred officers — the court merely used him against his talent."
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Wen told his aide Xi Chao, "Hao has learning and integrity. As a chief minister he could have guided the whole administration. The court simply misused him."

sentences.zh: 」將以浩為尚書令，以書告之。

translations.literal: He was about to make Hao Director of the Secretariat and informed him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: He now intended to restore him as Director of the Secretariat and sent word by letter.

sentences.zh: 浩欣然許焉，將答書，慮有謬誤，開閉者十數，竟達空函。

translations.literal: Hao gladly agreed; about to answer the letter, fearing error he opened and closed it more than ten times, and in the end delivered an empty envelope.
translations.idiomatic: Hao accepted with delight. Drafting his reply he fretted over every phrase, revising it again and again until he dispatched an envelope with nothing inside.

sentences.zh: 溫大怒，由是遂絕，卒於徙所。

translations.literal: Wen was greatly enraged; from this the connection was severed, and Hao died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was furious. The reconciliation died on the spot, and Hao ended his days in exile.

sentences.zh: 以前會稽內史王述為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: The former Interior Minister of Kuaiji Wang Shu was made Inspector of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, formerly interior minister of Kuaiji, was appointed inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，桓溫統步騎四萬發江陵。

translations.literal: Second month, day yichou: Huan Wen commanded forty thousand foot and horse and set out from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the second month Huan Wen marched from Jiangling at the head of forty thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 水軍自襄陽入均口，至南鄉，步兵自淅川趣武關，命司馬勳出子午道以伐秦。

translations.literal: The water force entered from Xiangyang through Jun Pass to Naxiang; infantry from Xichuan hastened toward Wu Pass; he ordered Sima Xun out by the Ziwu road to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His fleet advanced from Xiangyang through Jun Pass to Naxiang while his infantry struck for Wu Pass from Xichuan. Sima Xun was sent down the Ziwu Road to raid Qin.

sentences.zh: 燕衛將軍恪圍魯口，三月，拔之。

translations.literal: Yan Guard General Ke besieged Lukou; third month, he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke besieged Lukou and captured it in the third month.

sentences.zh: 呂護奔野王，遣弟奉表謝罪於燕，燕以護為河內太守。

translations.literal: Lv Hu fled to Yewang, sent his younger brother to submit a memorial asking pardon of Yan; Yan made Hu Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Lv Hu fled to Yewang and sent his brother to sue for mercy. Yan appointed him administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 姚襄遣使降燕。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang sent envoys to surrender to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang sent envoys offering submission to Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕主俊以慕容評為鎮南將軍，都督秦、雍、益、梁、江、揚、荊、徐、兗、豫十州諸軍事，權鎮洛水；

translations.literal: Yan ruler Jun made Murong Ping Pacifier of the South, commander over ten provinces' military affairs — Qin, Yong, Yi, Liang, Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xu, Yan, and Yu — with discretionary authority stationed on the Luo;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun named Murong Ping Pacifier of the South with nominal command over ten provinces and discretionary authority along the Luo River;

sentences.zh: 以慕容強為前鋒都督，督荊、徐二州、緣淮諸軍事，進據河南。

translations.literal: he made Murong Qiang vanguard commander, overseeing Jing and Xu and military affairs along the Huai, advancing to hold Henan south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: and put Murong Qiang in the vanguard to oversee the Huai front and seize the Henan region.

sentences.zh: 桓溫將攻上洛，獲秦荊州刺史郭敬；

translations.literal: Huan Wen was about to attack Shangluo and captured Qin Inspector of Jing Guo Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen moved against Shangluo and captured Former Qin's Jingzhou inspector Guo Jing;

sentences.zh: 進擊青泥，破之。

translations.literal: he advanced to strike Qingni and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: then stormed Qingni and broke through.

sentences.zh: 司馬勳掠秦西鄙，涼秦州刺史王擢攻陳倉以應溫。

translations.literal: Sima Xun raided Qin's western marches; Former Liang's Inspector of Qin Wang Zhuo attacked Chencang in response to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun raided the Qin west while Liang's Wang Zhuo attacked Chencang in coordination with Wen.

sentences.zh: 秦主健遣太子萇、丞相雄、淮南王生、平昌王菁、北平王碩帥眾五萬軍於嶢柳以拒溫。

translations.literal: Qin lord Jian sent Crown Prince Chang, Chancellor Xiong, Prince of Huainan Sheng, Prince of Pingchang Jing, and Prince of Beiping Shuo leading fifty thousand troops to encamp at Yaoliu to resist Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Crown Prince Fu Chang, Chancellor Fu Xiong, Prince Fu Sheng of Huainan, and other princes with fifty thousand men to camp at Yaoliu and block Wen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，已亥，溫與秦兵戰於藍田。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jihai: Wen fought Qin troops at Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jihai Wen met the Qin army at Lantian.

sentences.zh: 秦淮南王生單騎突陳，出入以十數，殺傷晉將士甚眾。

translations.literal: Qin's Prince of Huainan Sheng charged the line alone on horseback, going in and out a dozen times, killing and wounding very many Jin officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Sheng of Huainan charged alone through the Jin ranks a dozen times, slaughtering Jin troops wholesale.

sentences.zh: 溫督眾力戰，秦兵大敗；

translations.literal: Wen urged the host to fight fiercely; Qin troops suffered great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Wen drove his army hard and routed the Qin forces;

sentences.zh: 將軍桓沖又敗秦丞相雄於白鹿原。

translations.literal: General Huan Chong again defeated Qin Chancellor Xiong at Bailuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Huan Chong meanwhile crushed Chancellor Fu Xiong at Bailuyuan.

sentences.zh: 沖，溫之弟也。

translations.literal: Chong was Wen's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was Huan Wen's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 溫轉戰而前，壬寅，進至灞上。

translations.literal: Wen fought on as he advanced; on renyin he reached Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Wen fought his way forward and on renyin reached Bashang, at the gates of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦太子萇等退屯城南，秦主健與老弱六千固守長安小城，悉發精兵三萬，遣大司馬雷弱兒等與萇合兵以拒溫。

translations.literal: Qin Crown Prince Chang and the rest withdrew to camp south of the city; Qin lord Jian with six thousand aged and weak held the small city of Chang'an; he mustered all elite troops — thirty thousand — and sent Grand Marshal Lei Ruor and others to join Chang's force to resist Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Chang pulled back south of the city while Fu Jian held the inner walls of Chang'an with six thousand old men and civilians. Jian mustered thirty thousand picked troops and sent Grand Marshal Lei Ruor to reinforce the crown prince against Wen.

sentences.zh: 三輔郡縣皆來降，溫撫諭居民，使安堵復業。

translations.literal: All commanderies and counties of Sanfu came to surrender; Wen comforted and instructed the residents, enabling them to settle in peace and resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The counties of the capital region submitted. Wen reassured the people and set them back to their trades.

sentences.zh: 民爭持牛酒迎勞，男女夾路觀之，耆老有垂泣者，曰：「不圖今日復睹官軍！

translations.literal: The people vied to bring oxen and wine to welcome and refresh the troops; men and women lined the road to watch; among the elders some wept, saying: "Never did we dream that today we would again behold the government army!"
translations.idiomatic: Civilians rushed forward with cattle and wine, lining the roads as the army passed. Elders wept openly: "We never thought to see the imperial banners again in our lifetime!"

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄帥騎七千襲司馬勳於子午谷，破之，勳退屯女媧堡。

translations.literal: Qin Chancellor Xiong led seven thousand horse to raid Sima Xun in the Ziwu Valley, defeated him, and Xun withdrew to camp at Nüwa Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xiong struck Sima Xun in Ziwu Valley with seven thousand cavalry, broke him, and drove him back to Nüwa Fortress.

sentences.zh: 戊申，燕主俊封撫軍將軍軍為襄陽王，左將軍彭為武昌王；

translations.literal: On wushen Yan ruler Jun enfeoffed Suppressing-armies General Jun as Prince of Xiangyang and Left General Peng as Prince of Wuchang;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Murong Jun enfeoffed Murong Jun the Suppressing-armies General as Prince of Xiangyang and Murong Peng as Prince of Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 以衛將軍恪為大司馬、侍中、大都督、錄尚書事，封太原王；

translations.literal: he made Guard General Ke Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, Chief-commandant, and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffing him as Prince of Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: named Murong Ke Grand Marshal and Recorder of the Secretariat as Prince of Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍評為司徒、驃騎將軍，封上庸王；

translations.literal: Pacifier of the South Ping as Minister of Education and Flying-cavalry General, Prince of Shangyong;
translations.idiomatic: elevated Murong Ping to Minister of Education and Flying-cavalry General as Prince of Shangyong;

sentences.zh: 封安東將軍霸為吳王，左賢王友為范陽王，散騎常侍厲為下邳王，散騎常侍宜為廬江王，寧北將軍度為樂浪王；

translations.literal: he enfeoffed Pacifying-the-east General Ba as Prince of Wu, Left Worthy-king You as Prince of Fanyang, Regular Attendant Li as Prince of Xiapi, Regular Attendant Yi as Prince of Lujiang, and Pacifier of the North Du as Prince of Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: and raised a host of other kinsmen — Murong Ba as Prince of Wu among them, along with princes of Fanyang, Xiapi, Lujiang, and Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 又封弟桓為宜都王，逮為臨賀王，徽為河間王，龍為歷陽王，納為北海王，秀為蘭陵王，岳為安豐王，德為梁公，默為始安公，僂為南康公；

translations.literal: he also enfeoffed younger brothers Huan as Prince of Yidu, Dai as Prince of Linhe, Hui as Prince of Hejian, Long as Prince of Liyang, Na as Prince of Beihai, Xiu as Prince of Lanling, Yue as Prince of Anfeng, De as Duke of Liang, Mo as Duke of Shi'an, and Lou as Duke of Nankang;
translations.idiomatic: further ennobling younger brothers and cousins as princes and dukes across the realm;

sentences.zh: 子咸為樂安王，亮為勃海王，溫為帶方王，涉為漁陽王，暐為中山王；

translations.literal: his sons Xian as Prince of Lean, Liang as Prince of Bohai, Wen as Prince of Daifang, She as Prince of Yuyang, and Wei as Prince of Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: and investing his sons as kings of Lean, Bohai, Daifang, Yuyang, and Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 以尚書令陽騖為司空，仍守尚書令。

translations.literal: he made Director of the Secretariat Yang Gu Minister of Works while still holding the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gu became Minister of Works while retaining the directorate.

sentences.zh: 命冀州刺史吳王霸徙治信都。

translations.literal: He ordered Inspector of Ji Prince of Wu Ba to move his headquarters to Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ba was ordered to transfer his Ji provincial seat to Xindu.

sentences.zh: 初，燕王皝奇霸之才，故名之曰霸，將以為世子，群臣諫而止，然寵遇猶逾於世子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan king Huang had marveled at Ba's talent, therefore naming him Ba ("hegemon"), intending to make him heir; the ministers remonstrated and he stopped, yet favor still exceeded that of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang had once admired Ba so greatly that he named him Ba — "supremacy" — and nearly made him heir until the ministers dissuaded him, though favor still outshone the crown prince's.

sentences.zh: 由是俊惡之，以其嘗墜馬折齒，更名曰缺；

translations.literal: For this Jun hated him; because he had once fallen from a horse and broken teeth, he renamed him Que ("gap");
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun therefore disliked him, and after a fall that broke his teeth renamed him Que, "broken";

sentences.zh: 尋以其應讖文，更名曰垂；

translations.literal: soon because he matched a prophecy-text, renamed him Chui ("drooping");
translations.idiomatic: then, finding his name matched a prophecy, renamed him Chui;

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，錄留臺事，徙鎮龍城。

translations.literal: he was transferred to Palace Attendant, recorder of Eastern Capital affairs, and moved to garrison Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: promoted him to palace attendant to manage the eastern capital and posted him to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 垂大得東北之和，俊愈惡之，復召還。

translations.literal: Chui won great accord in the northeast; Jun hated him all the more and summoned him back again.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui won the wholehearted loyalty of the northeast, which only deepened Jun's suspicion and brought him back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，江西流民郭敞等千餘人執陳留內史劉仕，降於姚襄。

translations.literal: Fifth month: more than a thousand displaced people west of the river, Guo Chang and others, seized Interior Minister of Chenliu Liu Shi and surrendered to Yao Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month over a thousand refugees west of the Jiang seized Chenliu's interior minister Liu Shi and defected to Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 建康震駭，以吏部尚書周閔為中軍將軍，屯中堂，豫州刺史謝尚自歷陽還衛京師，固江備守。

translations.literal: Jiankang was shaken in terror; Minister of Personnel Zhou Min was made Central Army General and encamped at Zhongtang; Inspector of Yu Xie Shang returned from Liyang to guard the capital and strengthened the river defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The capital panicked. Zhou Min was named Central Army General and posted to Zhongtang while Xie Shang rushed back from Liyang to defend Jiankang and fortify the river line.

sentences.zh: 王擢拔陳倉，殺秦扶風內史毛難。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuo took Chencang and killed Mao Nan, Interior Minister of Fufeng in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo seized Chencang and killed Qin's Fufeng interior minister Mao Nan.

sentences.zh: 北海王猛，少好學，倜儻有大志，不屑細務，人皆輕之。

translations.literal: Wang Meng of Beihai loved learning in his youth; he was free-spirited with great ambition, disdained petty affairs, and everyone looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng of Beihai was a gifted student with bold ambitions who scorned petty work, and most people underestimated him.

sentences.zh: 猛悠然自得，隱居華陰。

translations.literal: Meng lived at ease and in seclusion at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He lived contentedly in seclusion at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 聞桓溫入關，披褐詣之，捫虱而談當世之務，旁若無人。

translations.literal: When he heard that Huan Wen had entered the passes, he put on coarse cloth and went to him, picking lice as he discussed the affairs of the age, as if no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Huan Wen had entered the passes, he went to him in humble dress, picking lice as he discussed statecraft as though they were alone in the room.

sentences.zh: 溫異之，問曰：「吾奉天子之命，將銳兵十萬為百姓除殘賊，而三秦豪傑未有至者，何也？

translations.literal: Wen was struck by him and asked, "I bear the Son of Heaven's command, leading a hundred thousand sharp troops to rid the people of cruel bandits—why have none of the worthies of the Three Qin come to me?
translations.idiomatic: Wen was impressed and asked, "I march at the emperor's order with a hundred thousand men to destroy the oppressors—why have the leaders of the Three Qin not come to me?

sentences.zh: 」猛曰：「公不遠數千里，深入敵境。

translations.literal: Meng said, "My lord has come thousands of li, deep into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: Meng answered, "You have marched thousands of li into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 今長安咫尺，而不渡灞水，百姓未知公心，所以不至。

translations.literal: Chang'an is now within a stone's throw, yet you do not cross the Ba River—the people do not yet know your heart, and that is why they have not come."
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an is almost in sight, yet you will not cross the Ba River. The people do not yet know your intent—that is why they stay away."

sentences.zh: 」溫嘿然無以應，徐曰：「江東無卿比也！

translations.literal: Wen was silent and had no reply; after a pause he said, "East of the river there is no one to compare with you!
translations.idiomatic: Wen fell silent, then said slowly, "There is no one like you in the southeast!

sentences.zh: 」乃署猛軍謀祭酒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Meng Libationer for Military Planning.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Meng libationer for military planning.

sentences.zh: 溫與秦丞相雄等戰於白鹿原，溫兵不利，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Wen fought Qin Chancellor Xiong and others at Bailu Plain; Wen's army fared badly and more than ten thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: Wen fought Qin chancellor Fu Xiong at Bailu Plain and lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 初，溫指秦麥以為糧，既而秦人悉芟麥，清野以待之，溫軍乏食。

translations.literal: Earlier Wen had counted on Qin wheat for provisions; then the Qin people cut down all the wheat and cleared the countryside to await him, and Wen's army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had counted on Qin wheat for supplies, but the Qin stripped the fields bare and his army went hungry.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁丑，徙關中三千餘戶而歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingchou, he moved more than three thousand households from Guanzhong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day dingchou, he relocated more than three thousand Guanzhong households and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以王猛為高官督護，欲與俱還，猛辭不就。

translations.literal: He made Wang Meng a senior supervising officer and wished him to return together; Meng declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He offered Wang Meng a senior post and asked him to return east; Meng refused.

sentences.zh: 呼延毒帥眾一萬從溫還。

translations.literal: Huyan Du led ten thousand followers and returned with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan Du withdrew with Wen at the head of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 秦太子萇等隨溫擊之，比至潼關，溫軍屢敗，失亡以萬數。

translations.literal: Qin Crown Prince Chang and others pursued Wen and struck him; by the time they reached Tong Pass, Wen's army had been repeatedly defeated and losses numbered in the tens of thousands.
