translations.idiomatic: Qin crown prince Chang pursued him; by Tong Pass Wen had lost battle after battle and tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 溫之屯灞上也，順陽太守薛珍勸溫徑進逼長安，溫弗從。

translations.literal: When Wen was encamped at Ba, Shunyang Administrator Xue Zhen urged Wen to advance directly and press Chang'an; Wen would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: While Wen camped at Ba, Shunyang prefect Xue Zhen urged a direct march on Chang'an; Wen refused.

sentences.zh: 珍以偏師獨濟，頗有所獲。

translations.literal: Zhen crossed alone with a detached force and gained considerable booty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen crossed with a detached force on his own and won some gains.

sentences.zh: 及溫退，乃還，顯言於眾，自矜其勇而咎溫之持重；

translations.literal: When Wen withdrew, he then returned and spoke openly to the crowd, praising his own courage and blaming Wen's caution;
translations.idiomatic: After Wen withdrew, Zhen returned and boasted publicly of his courage while blaming Wen's caution;

sentences.zh: 溫殺之。

translations.literal: Wen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had him executed.

sentences.zh: 秦丞相雄擊司馬勳、王擢於陳倉，勳奔漢中，擢奔略陽。

translations.literal: Qin Chancellor Xiong attacked Sima Xun and Wang Zhuo at Chencang; Xun fled to Hanzhong and Zhuo fled to Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin chancellor Fu Xiong attacked Sima Xun and Wang Zhuo at Chencang; Xun fled to Hanzhong and Zhuo to Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 秦以光祿大夫趙俱為洛陽刺史，鎮宜陽。

translations.literal: Qin appointed Palace Counselor Zhao Ju Inspector of Luoyang, garrisoning Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin made palace counselor Zhao Ju Luoyang inspector at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 秦東海敬武王雄攻喬秉於雍；

translations.literal: Qin's Revered Martial King of Donghai, Xiong, attacked Qiao Bing at Yong;
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Revered Martial King of Donghai, Fu Xiong, attacked Qiao Bing at Yong;

sentences.zh: 丙申，卒。

translations.literal: on the day bingshen he died.
translations.idiomatic: and on the day bingshen he died.

sentences.zh: 秦主健哭之嘔血，曰：「天不欲吾平四海邪？

translations.literal: Qin ruler Jian wept for him until he vomited blood, saying, "Does Heaven not wish me to pacify the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Jian wept until he vomited blood and cried, "Does Heaven not want me to unite the realm?

sentences.zh: 何奪吾元才之速也！

translations.literal: Why take Yuan Cai from me so soon!
translations.idiomatic: Why take Yuan Cai from me so soon!

sentences.zh: 」贈魏王，葬禮依晉安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and funeral rites followed the precedent of Jin's Prince Xian of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously created Prince of Wei with funeral honors matching Jin's Prince Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 雄以佐命無勳，位兼將相，權侔人主，而謙恭泛愛，遵奉法度，故健重之，常曰：「元才，吾之周公也。

translations.literal: Though Xiong had no merit in establishing the mandate, he held both general and ministerial rank and power equal to a sovereign, yet was humble, broadly loving, and observant of law—therefore Jian valued him and often said, "Yuan Cai is my Duke of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiong had not helped found the dynasty, he held both civil and military power equal to the throne, yet remained humble and law-abiding. Jian treasured him and often said, "Yuan Cai is my Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」子堅襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu Jian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 堅性至孝，幼有志度，博學多能，交結英豪，呂婆樓、強汪及略陽梁平老皆與之善。

translations.literal: Jian was supremely filial by nature; from youth he had resolve and measure, was learned and capable in many arts, and befriended heroes—Lü Polou, Qiang Wang, and Liang Pinglao of Lueyang were all on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was deeply filial, ambitious from youth, learned and capable, and drew heroes to him—including Lü Polou, Qiang Wang, and Liang Pinglao of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 燕樂陵太守慕容鉤，翰之子也，與青州刺史朱禿共治厭次。

translations.literal: Murong Gou, Administrator of Leling in Yan and son of Han, jointly governed Yanci with Zhu Tu, Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gou, Leling prefect and son of Murong Han, governed Yanci jointly with Qing inspector Zhu Tu.

sentences.zh: 鉤自恃宗室，每陵侮禿，禿不勝忿。

translations.literal: Gou relied on his imperial clan status and constantly insulted Tu; Tu could not bear the anger.
translations.idiomatic: Gou bullied Zhu Tu on the strength of his royal blood until Tu could endure no more.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，襲鉤，殺之，南奔段龕。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, he attacked Gou by surprise, killed him, and fled south to Duan Kan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, he ambushed and killed Gou, then fled south to Duan Kan.

sentences.zh: 秦太子萇攻喬秉於雍。

translations.literal: Qin Crown Prince Chang attacked Qiao Bing at Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Qin crown prince Chang attacked Qiao Bing at Yong.

sentences.zh: 八月，斬之，關中悉平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he beheaded him, and Guanzhong was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he executed him, and Guanzhong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 秦主健賞拒桓溫之功，以雷弱兒為丞相，毛貴為太傅，魚遵為太尉，淮南王生為中軍大將軍，平昌王菁為司空。

translations.literal: Qin ruler Jian rewarded the merit of repelling Huan Wen: Lei Ruo'er was made Chancellor, Mao Gui Grand Tutor, Yu Zun Grand Commandant, Prince of Huainan Sheng Central Army Grand General, and Prince of Pingchang Jing Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jian rewarded those who had repelled Huan Wen: Lei Ruo'er became chancellor, Mao Gui grand tutor, Yu Zun grand commandant, Prince of Huainan Sheng central army commander, and Prince of Pingchang Jing minister of works.

sentences.zh: 健勤於政事，數延公卿咨講治道，承趙人苛虐奢侈之後，易以寬簡節儉，崇儒禮士，由是秦人悅之。

translations.literal: Jian was diligent in government affairs, often summoning dukes and ministers to consult on the way of rule; succeeding the harsh cruelty and extravagance of the Zhao people, he replaced them with leniency, simplicity, and thrift, honored Confucianism and treated scholars with ritual—thereby the people of Qin were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian worked tirelessly at government, consulting his ministers often. After Zhao's cruelty and excess, he ruled with leniency and thrift, honored learning and scholars, and won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 燕大調兵眾，因發詔之日，號曰：「丙戌舉。

translations.literal: Yan made a great levy of troops; because of the day the edict was issued, it was called the "Bingxu levy."
translations.idiomatic: Yan mobilized on a vast scale; because the edict went out on the day bingxu, men called it the "Bingxu levy."

sentences.zh: 九月，桓溫還自伐秦，帝遣侍中、黃門勞溫於襄陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Huan Wen returned from campaigning against Qin; the emperor sent an Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Attendant to comfort Wen at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Huan Wen returned from his Qin campaign; the emperor sent courtiers to welcome him at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 或告燕黃門侍郎宋斌等謀奉冉智為主而反，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yan Palace Attendant Song Bin and others plotted to set up Ran Zhi as leader and rebel; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Yan attendant Song Bin and others of plotting to restore Ran Zhi; all were executed.

sentences.zh: 斌，燭之子也。

translations.literal: Bin was the son of Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was Zhu's son.

sentences.zh: 秦太子萇之拒桓溫也，為流矢所中，冬，十月，卒，謚曰獻哀。

translations.literal: When Qin Crown Prince Chang had resisted Huan Wen he was struck by a stray arrow; in winter, the tenth month, he died, with posthumous title Lamented Offering.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Chang, wounded by a stray arrow while fighting Huan Wen, died in winter, the tenth month, and was posthumously titled Lamented Offering.

sentences.zh: 燕王俊如龍城。

translations.literal: Murong Jun of Yan went to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ruler Jun traveled to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓溫之入關也，王擢遣使告涼王祚，言溫善用兵，其志難測。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen entered the passes, Wang Zhuo sent envoys to tell Liang King Zuo that Wen was skilled in warfare and his intentions hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen entered the passes, Wang Zhuo warned Liang ruler Zhang Zuo that Wen was a formidable commander whose aims were unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 祚懼，且畏擢之叛己，遣人刺之。

translations.literal: Zuo was afraid, and also feared that Zhuo would rebel against him, and sent men to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo, alarmed and fearing Zhuo might turn against him, sent assassins.

sentences.zh: 事洩，祚益懼，大發兵，聲言東伐，實欲西保敦煌，會溫還而止。

translations.literal: The plot leaked; Zuo grew more afraid, mobilized troops on a large scale, proclaimed an eastern campaign while in truth intending to secure himself at Dunhuang in the west—he stopped when Wen returned.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed. Terrified, Zuo mobilized, claiming an eastern campaign while planning to flee west to Dunhuang—until Wen withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既而遣秦州刺史牛霸等帥兵三千擊擢，破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Qin Province Inspector Niu Ba and others leading three thousand troops to attack Zhuo and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Qin inspector Niu Ba with three thousand men against Zhuo and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，擢帥眾降秦，秦以擢為尚書，以上將軍啖鐵為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zhuo led his followers in surrender to Qin; Qin made Zhuo Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Supreme General Tietie Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhuo submitted to Qin, which made him director of the secretariat and supreme general Tietie Qin inspector.

sentences.zh: 秦王健叔父武都王安自晉還，為姚襄所虜，以為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian's uncle, Prince of Wudu An, returning from Jin, was captured by Yao Xiang and made Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's uncle, Prince of Wudu An, returning from Jin, was captured by Yao Xiang and made Luo inspector.

sentences.zh: 十二月，安亡歸秦，健以安為大司馬、驃騎大將軍、并州刺史，鎮蒲板。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month An escaped back to Qin; Jian made An Grand Marshal, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Bing Province, garrisoning Puban.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month An escaped back to Qin; Jian made him grand marshal, flying cavalry grand general, and Bing inspector at Puban.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦大饑，米一升直布一匹。

translations.literal: That year Qin suffered great famine; one sheng of rice was worth one bolt of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin suffered famine so severe that a liter of rice cost a whole bolt of cloth.
